issues.title: Executed-agreement recorder files against an implicit Operator instance on multi-instance clients
issues.body:
## The gap

The executed-agreement recorder shipped in #2644 binds to a single Operator instance per client hub, chosen implicitly:

- `src/pages/admin/clients/[id].astro:48` — `const operator = roster.find((r) => r.entity_id === entityId) ?? null`. The roster is ordered `customer_slug ASC`, so this is "whichever instance sorts first alphabetically."
- `src/pages/admin/clients/[id].astro:326` — the upload form posts `instanceSlug={operator.customer_slug}`, so every document filed from that hub lands on that one instance.
- The hub's list reads `listOperatorAgreementDocumentsForEntity` (all instances for the entity) and renders each row without naming the instance it belongs to.

So on a multi-instance client, an admin can file a firm's executed agreement against the wrong Operator instance and get no signal that they did, and cannot tell from the list which instance any existing document belongs to.

## Not hypothetical

Prod D1, checked 2026-08-29:

```
SELECT entity_id, COUNT(*) FROM customer_configs GROUP BY entity_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
→ f03ffe58-db0d-47bb-a409-922a7ee62ea7  |  4
```

That is the SMD dogfood entity, which holds four Operator instances today. Ashton & Price holds one, so the first real client is unaffected.

## Blast radius: admin-side only

The client-facing half is correct and does not need changing. `listOperatorAgreementDocuments` queries `(entity_id, instance_slug)` and the Compliance route passes its own `instance`, so an instance's page can only ever show its own paper. No client can be shown another instance's documents.

The failure mode is a **filing accident**, not a disclosure one: the document lands on an instance whose Compliance page the firm may never open, and nothing tells anyone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The client hub's record-document form carries an explicit instance selector when the entity has more than one Operator instance, defaulting to nothing rather than to an alphabetical accident.
- [ ] Each row in the hub's document list names the instance it belongs to.
- [ ] A single-instance client's form is unchanged (no selector, no extra click) — this must not tax the common case.
- [ ] Test coverage for the multi-instance case: a document filed against instance B does not appear on instance A's portal read.

## Notes

The endpoint already refuses an `instance_slug` that does not belong to the entity (`recordDocument` checks `getCustomerConfigBySlug(...).entity_id`), so this is about choosing the RIGHT instance among a client's own, not about cross-tenant safety.

Found while answering whether #2644 was built as a product feature or for one client. It is a product feature; this is the one place it is not yet fully general.

issues.title: EPIC: routine 11 medical chronology as a durable, profitable Operator routine (document deliverable, on-Machine runner, contract limits)
issues.body:
## Mission

Routine 11 (Medical chronology) delivers the chronology document the firm has been receiving from the laptop pipeline, as a routine, inside the flat fee, without the Captain in the loop, with contract limits that keep it profitable.

Design (team synthesis + economics appendix, 2026-08-27): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c

## Decisions recorded (Captain, 2026-08-27)

- **Topology**: the pipeline runs on the firm's own Machine, upsized, as a root-owned supervised job. No laptop, no sibling Machine, no R2 (agreement §4.2 and the DPA keep matter content on the dedicated Machine; the OAuth relay restarts every Machine in the app).
- **Content control (option a)**: the filed chronology document set moves connector-side and is not inspected by the trust plugin's identifier/citation gates; the runner's own gates (full claim audit, extractive sweep, cross-client page gate, matter-provenance gate) are the registered control. ADR lands in slice 2.
- **Product shape**: build on a Named Administrator's request; keep current automatically on matters that carry a chronology; the running memo is the human-readable index and covered-set record.
- **Economics**: the margin lever is removing the Captain from the run ($800-1,600 labor per chronology today vs $20-80 tokens); allowance measured in pages; per-matter gate; overage in 500-doc blocks at $1.00/doc.

## Slices (in order; each shippable and observable)

| # | Issue | Size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #2439 memo gate: pointer-style memo so the running record can land | S |
| 2 | #2611 ADR + firm settings block + runtime-control registration | S |
| 3 | #2612 seat upsize (template renders cpus) | S |
| 4 | #2613 pipeline as an SMD-owned package with machine gates and cents ledger | L |
| 5 | #2614 on-Machine runner: supervisor, queue, broker verbs, audit, cost plane (spans overlay) | L |
| 6 | #2615 connector deliver_artifact_set, .msg (#2465), extract-cache write-back | M |
| 7 | #2616 skill rewrite (build/append/deliver) + triggers; first production delivery by the routine | M |
| 8 | #2617 contract limits, routine card, handbook, Captain skill | S |

Slice 8's contract wording must reach the firm before §2.8 is relied on; Chris returns 2026-09-08.

## Done means

- [ ] (runtime) An administrator's emailed request produces a chronology folder on a real A&P matter with no laptop involved; `crane_verify` ids for resolution and folder read-back
- [ ] (runtime) A new record landing on that matter produces an append run that reads only the new pages
- [ ] Three runner-executed jobs reconcile at or under $0.45/doc against console receipts
- [ ] The signed agreement carries the row-11 limits

## Open probes (design §7)

Page census for the allowance figure; memo gate accepts pointer style; job worker claims every row (confirms the separate queue); Batch API timing at real PNG sizes; effort lever benchmark; memory headroom on 4 GB; `machine.size` rendering; workspace attribution live; `files.updated` payload; counsel read on the §4.2 sentence; presigned URL lifetime.

issues.title: routine 11 slice 8: contract limits (pages, per-matter gate, overage), routine card, handbook, Captain skill
issues.body:
Slice 8 of the routine-11 productization: the paper and the docs. Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c §4 and the economics appendix §7.

The agreement files live in the PRIVATE engagements repo (`operator/customers/ashton-price/agreements/`); this issue tracks the change from ss-console because the routine card, handbook, and Captain skill change here in the same wave. Client-facing wording is Captain-authored; the items below are the content, not the copy.

## Contract (engagements, Captain-edited before §2.8 goes to the firm; Chris returns 09-08)

1. **Exhibit A row 11**: measure in **pages** (documents as the plain-English gloss); refresh counts only new pages; the "fifteen to twenty chronologies" parenthetical becomes "roughly ten to fifteen on matters of the size seen to date". Allowance figure set by the page census (probe 2 in the design).
2. **Per-matter gate**: 400 medical documents or 3,000 exhibit pages, whichever first; above it the Operator surfaces the count and stops; SMD quotes that matter alone.
3. **Build-on-request only** for the document; keep-current is automatic on matters that carry one.
4. **Overage**: 500-document blocks at $1.00/doc, accepted in writing first; no carryover (already §2.8).
5. **Permanent caps / Schedule A-1 row 11**: "internal record" now names the running memo AND the filed chronology document set; never sent outside the firm; never characterizes.
6. **§4.2 one sentence** regularizing the bounded, expiring on-Machine transcription cache; DPA Exhibit B-1 Fly row amended to match. Counsel read on whether it is a sub-processor change (30-day notice).
7. Internal, not contractual: unit cost > $0.60/doc for two months triggers §2.7 re-scope; $7,500 tier with 5,000-doc allowance is the shape for a 30/month firm.

## ss-console

- `docs/handbook/` page for routine 11 (maintenance contract)
- `docs/skills/medchron/SKILL.md` becomes the Captain-side submitter/reader of runner jobs; RUNBOOK Step 5 laptop transport retired (engagements)
- `routine-grid.yaml` wording aligned with the sent card

## Acceptance

- [ ] §2.8 letter sent to the firm with the above (Captain act; message id recorded in the dossier)
- [ ] Signature copies carry the row-11 wording
- [ ] Handbook integrity test green

Size: S.

issues.title: routine 11 slice 7: skill rewrite (build / append / deliver) and triggers
issues.body:
Slice 7 of the routine-11 productization. Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c §1, §2, §7 probes 1, 9.

## What lands

1. **Skill rewrite** `operator/skills/medical-chronology-maintainer/` with three modes:
   - **build** (Named Administrator request by email or Claude connector): dual-probe matter resolution, folder selection reported as prose to the requester (unmatched folder → ask), allowance pre-flight, `medchron_job_submit`.
   - **append** (new records on a matter that already carries a chronology): delta = `get_files_on_matter` minus the document set recorded in the last memo/manifest; reads only new pages.
   - **deliver** (on handoff wake): pointer-style memo (chronology folder + sha + covered count), `create_task` for the responsible attorney, reply to the requester with counts, exclusions, and any held question; confirm-by-read on every write.
2. **Triggers**: `customer.yaml` initiation `manual + webhook`; `webhook_triggers` entry for `smokeball files.updated` only after the payload is verified on the tenant (probe 9); until then a per-skill cron delta gate `pre_run_medchron.py` (the shared template is explicitly not per-skill), registered in `operator/contracts/pre-run-shared-symbols.json`.
3. `routine-grid.yaml` row 11: initiation string and notes updated; exposure unchanged (`internal_write: autonomous`); ceiling verbatim unchanged.
4. Test cases: build/append/deliver fixtures; selector test updated.

## Acceptance

- [ ] (runtime) First production chronology delivered by the routine on a real administrator request, no laptop involved; `crane_verify` ids for resolution and folder read-back
- [ ] (runtime) One append run on that matter reads only the new documents (ledger page count proves it)
- [ ] Laptop pipeline retired from delivery after this lands (RUNBOOK Step 5 removed in slice 8)

Size: M. Depends on slices 2-6.

issues.title: routine 11 slice 6: connector deliver_artifact_set, .msg extraction with work-product fence, extract-cache write-back
issues.body:
Slice 6 of the routine-11 productization. Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c §2 (write path), §4 (cache).

## What lands (in `operator/connectors/smokeball/smokeball_connector/`)

1. **`deliver_artifact_set`**: port of `seat_write_deliverable.py:88-131` into the connector: refuse if target folder exists, `create_folder`, `add_file` per file after sha re-check, sleep, folder read-back with byte counts (`file_id: null` is not confirmation). Never deletes; a superseding run writes a new dated folder. Both underlying calls are already `INTERNAL_WRITE`. Output-class binding for `medical-chronology-maintainer` gains `smokeball_file` (`output-classes.yaml`).
2. **`.msg` extraction** with the work-product fence (closes #2465 for this lane): attachments folded by sha, `.rpmsg` reported as its own bucket, firm intake/valuation notes excluded and named.
3. **Extract-cache write-back** (`extract_cache.py`): sha-keyed transcriptions written by the runner; bound raised to a Captain-authored size/TTL. This is the only cross-job text reuse and it needs the §4.2 sentence in slice 8 before it turns on for A&P.

## Acceptance

- [ ] (runtime) Folder read-back with byte counts on a rehearsal matter; `crane_verify` id
- [ ] `record_check` no longer refuses `.msg`-heavy matters
- [ ] Cache bound and TTL are config, not constants; boot smoke asserts them

Size: M. Related: #2465, #2464, #2466.

issues.title: routine 11 slice 5: on-Machine medchron runner (root supervisor, queue, broker verbs, audit, cost plane)
issues.body:
Slice 5 of the routine-11 productization. Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c §2 (dispatch seam, state model, audit trail).

Spans ss-console AND hermes-smd-overlay; not shipped until both land and `OVERLAY_REF` is bumped.

## What lands

1. **Runner image layer** (overlay Dockerfile): poppler, pymupdf, matplotlib, extract-msg, python-docx, anthropic; the slice-4 package vendored at a pinned sha.
2. **Root supervisor + queue** (overlay, `config_applier` pattern): `medchron-runner` under tini, `nice 10`, memory-capped cgroup, drops to a dedicated `medchron` uid; watches `/opt/data/medchron/queue/`; workdir `/opt/data/medchron/jobs/<job>/` wiped after delivery + 72 h. One job at a time, FIFO. This is NOT the Hermes job ledger (the in-process worker claims every claimable row, `shared/job_worker.py`).
3. **Broker verbs** `medchron_job_submit` / `medchron_job_status` / `medchron_allowance` (overlay `workspace_broker/`): root validates matter id + number + client names from the seat's dual-probe resolution, mode, file ids, selection digest, cents cap, requester. Mapped `INTERNAL_WRITE` in `shared/action_classes.py` (unmapped tools are refused).
4. **Audit**: every state transition (`submitted`, `held`, `running`, `delivered`, `failed`) via `audit_append`; delivery row carries folder id, shas, byte counts, pages, cents. Vocabulary in `operator/contracts/audit-action-vocabulary.json`.
5. **Cost plane**: same workspace key as the seat so the nightly ingest attributes it (ADR 0062 §2); routine-11 spend is kept OUT of the daily `sticky_stop` ladder (one $80 job would hard-stop the seat).
6. **Runtime-read kind** `medchron_jobs` (counts, states, cents, pages; never content) + console admin page.
7. Handoff wake on completion via the existing `/webhooks/handoff` (source seat-local) so the agent's deliver mode runs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] (runtime) A submitted job on a rehearsal matter runs to `delivered` on the pilot seat; `crane_verify` id
- [ ] Console page shows counts; nightly ingest shows the workspace spend for the run
- [ ] Boot smoke asserts the runner is idle-cheap and the queue dir is root-owned
- [ ] Seat stays healthy through a full job (Fly metrics captured)

Size: L.

issues.title: routine 11 slice 4: the medchron pipeline becomes an SMD-owned package with machine gates and a cents ledger
issues.body:
Slice 4 of the routine-11 productization. Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4f3dc2e4-65af-4423-a130-995a604af97c §2 (components), §3 (levers), §5 (gates).

## What lands

The ~40 laptop scripts (private engagements repo `operator/customers/ashton-price/tools/medchron/`) become an SMD-owned package at `operator/runners/medchron/` with a fixed DAG, machine verdicts per gate, and no human gates.

1. **DAG**: download → extract → index_msg (fold by sha, `.rpmsg` disclosed, work-product fence) → vision (Batch API) → build_units → billing → map (Batch, per-document chunks, 128k output; no designed-in truncation) → assemble → merge → group → filter_preincident → exhibits → condense → summarize → build_doc → classify/strip (`--falsify` first) → coverage_gate → audit loop (sync, cached page images, blind reader, full-range) → check_exhibits → extractive gate → cross-client gate → provenance gate → render docx → manifest.
2. **Gates as code** (design §5, 1-13): any FAIL/HOLD writes nothing. New: cross-client page gate (patient-header scan + controlled vision on scans), provenance gate (matter number, client, incident date must equal the envelope; every entry date resolves to a cited page). `check_exhibits` promoted into the DAG with its known-bad v2 fixture.
3. **Ledger**: cents from one price table, `cache_creation`, request/batch ids, document sha, page and claim grain; refuses unattributed rows; per-job cents cap enforced before every paid stage; page counter reported.
4. **Levers with evidence**: Batch API for vision/map/billing; audit sync with page-image caching; pre-vision dedupe of rescans and name-excluded vendor files. Effort lever NOT adopted until the Modellas benchmark re-runs at ≥95% agreement / 100% UNSUPPORTED recall.
5. Firm settings from slice 2 replace constants (`group_providers.py:28-50`, `timeline.py:19,22-30`).
6. Known-bad control fixtures in CI for gates 8, 10, 11, 12.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Package reproduces one calibration matter byte-for-byte in every gate's verdict on a laptop before it runs on a seat
- [ ] Each known-bad fixture fails its gate in CI
- [ ] Ledger reconciles against console receipts within 10% on a calibration run
- [ ] engagements `tools/medchron/` frozen at the vendored sha (README note there; laptop pipeline stays the oracle until slice 7)

Size: L.

issues.title: A deadline alarm can record itself as rung: escalation `fired` has no send precondition
issues.body:
## What happens

`operator/workspace_broker/escalation_ledger.py::validate_append` guards `acked`
— its docstring says *"you cannot ack an alarm that never rang"* — and has **no
branch for `fired`/`chased` at all**. The ack is fenced against forgery; the
raise is not. A forged raise silences the alarm just as effectively, because
`should_fire` reads `last_raised_date` off a raise row and `refire_days` does
the rest.

Observed on pilot-smokeball:

- **2026-08-26T14:00Z** — woke on 5 needs-you items, derived 5 ACK codes, made
  ONE delivery attempt (`create_memo`, refused by the cross-matter fence), wrote
  **5 `fired` rows**, ended the turn. Zero send-tool calls, though
  `smd_send_message` was available and this skill used it 16 times this month.
  Those 5 real overdue deadlines are suppressed until 2026-08-29.
  `vfy_01M0ZNJT2BTHGVZ5WQCBP1TVPZ`
- **2026-08-20T14:00Z** — **77 appends, zero sends**, no memo refusal anywhere.
  The turn called the `smd_deliver_draft` *authorization* gate, got `ok`, and
  never delivered. `vfy_01M0ZRQYEJ1K23Y2RN5HQ0V3D5`

**Since 2026-08-01 the routine delivered on 4 days out of 23.** The Captain has
been receiving `[SMD Ops] send refused: unsent/no_send_attempted` pages — the
ss#2547 pager working correctly. It reports the smaller half: the pager sees the
silence, nothing stops the ledger recording a delivery that did not happen.

Note the pager surfaces only its newest events, so "no alert" is not "nothing
was missed"; the history is only visible by querying the ledger.

The rule is already doctrine — `references/algorithm.md`: *"If the send did not
happen, write nothing... Never report an item as raised unless the send AND the
ledger write both succeeded."* Prose addressed to the model is not a control.

## Reachability contract (`/wired`)

**Sentence:** A person at the firm whose deadline is overdue receives the
escalation alert; when a run fails to deliver, the next scheduled run raises it
again instead of the item going silent for `refire_days`.

**Terminal seam:** the recipient's mailbox on the tick *after* a delivery-less run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (repo) `validate_append` refuses a `fired`/`chased` the broker did not witness dispatching to a non-probe recipient, via a required `send_witness` keyword with no default
- [x] (repo) The witness reuses the overlay `_dispatched_to_a_person` semantics (a `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED` with a recipient not prefixed `ss-probe`), so the control and the `no_send_attempted` pager cannot disagree about the same run
- [x] (repo) The raise is joined to the dispatch on `session_id`, not a wall-clock window
- [x] (repo) A retro-falsifier replays real August rows and both allows the four days that delivered and refuses 08-26 and 08-25T18:32
- [x] (repo) The escalator skill names the tool that actually delivers
- [x] (repo) The twin pair is restamped across the canonical, its five vendored skill copies, and the overlay
- [ ] (runtime) The running broker on pilot-smokeball carries the change
- [ ] (runtime) An unwitnessed `fired` is refused on the live seat
- [ ] (runtime) A real overdue item is delivered to a mailbox on the following tick

## Scope note

The control stops the ledger lying about delivery. It does **not** make the
escalator send — the 08-20 turn will still need to actually deliver. The last AC
is deliberately separate for that reason and must be reported unmet if it is
unmet; reprovisioning does not stand in for it.

Delivery reliability itself (the pattern of completing the ceremony around
delivery without delivering) is larger than a skill-copy edit and wants its own
issue.

## Proof note

A one-shot `hermes cron create --skill ... --script ...` reproduces composition
faithfully but **not** delivery — it composes and files locally, so it looks
like this bug even when the bug is absent. The managed job (or the shadow-firm
rehearsal) is the only faithful driver for the send leg.

issues.title: Message format is a binding class property: the structure tier is built, the template tier is not (refiles #2090)
issues.body:
Refiles #2090 with current evidence, as that issue's own closing comment invited: *"This is not a verdict on the content. If it does [still hold], refile it with what you observed."*

It still holds. #2090 was filed 2026-07-30, never picked up, and closed 2026-08-24 20:56 by the backlog flush with all five ACs unchecked and `force-close` applied so the unmet-AC gate could not reopen it. **The digest broke the next morning.**

## What was observed

The pilot's 2026-08-25 07:00 run sent scott@smd.services a deadline digest of 4,280 characters whose only markdown block marker was a single `---`. Every identifier in it was correct — that half is the ss#2390 proof, `vfy_01M0WMTQ5B3X8D92K3XQ2TJDEX`. Its shape was not: no headings, no list items, every band collapsed into one run-on paragraph, 38 escalation rows flat with 20 of them for one matter, and a projection field name reaching the reader as the English word "authored" on a court date one day out. `vfy_01M0WM79FKAXEC3EJA3TNTMB3Y`.

The send-path audit row read `output_class=staff, reason=no_spec, rules=["voice"]`. Voice was the only thing checked.

## Scope, corrected by exploration

#2090 said "37 skills carry `references/output-format.md`". True, but most produce documents (drafting lane) or internal memos. **5 skills compose messages that reach a send path**, carrying two families:

| Family | Skills |
|---|---|
| `banded_digest` | `deadline-miss-escalator`, `daily-needs-you-digest` |
| `decision_card` | `client-verification-tracker`, `medical-records-chaser`, `new-matter-intake` |

`inbox-triage` never sends (SKILL.md: *"Never sends… there is no send tool in this skill's surface"*), and `connector-auth-check` / `workspace` compose nothing.

## Done: the check tier

overlay#323 — the structure floor. Three mechanical rules (`no_heading`, `no_list_items`, `paragraph_wall`), one call site in `evaluate_tool_call` outside the `decision.allowed` guard, family resolved from `cron_attribution`, `staff` proceeds-and-alerts while outbound routes to a human. 31 tests, both instruments confirmed able to fail.

It asserts mechanics only — never which sections exist, what they are called, or in what order. Per ADR 0037 tenet 3 and ADR 0083 §3, the format itself stays the customer's.

## Still open: the template tier, which is what makes format configurable

This is the half that closes ADR 0083's two unchecked ACs:

- `(repo) A customer statement of format becomes a stored class property`
- `(runtime) A delivered digest is observed honoring a customer-authored format, and honoring it identically on a second run`

**Smaller than it looks — the storage and delivery already exist.** `shared/spec_manifest.py`'s `SpecEntry` already carries an `assertions` field per output class and property, and `spec_applier` already pulls `vaults/<slug>/output-classes.json` from R2, hash-verifies it, installs it root-owned, and commits a digest-stamped manifest the agent cannot write.

The gap is the vocabulary. `shared/format_check.py`'s `KNOWN_ASSERTIONS` is a closed set of six — `opening_line_prefix`, `closing_line_prefix`, `single_closing_line`, `forbid_bullets`, `forbid_substrings`, `max_chars` — and **none can express structure**; `forbid_bullets` is the inverse of what a digest needs. Growing it is a two-repo act, seat first, or a rule the console offers is silently ignored while the client believes it is enforced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (repo) A structure floor rejects a message that carries no blocks — overlay#323
- [x] (repo) The floor runs on a `draft_for_review` seat, not only an autonomous one — overlay#323
- [x] (repo) `staff` proceeds and alerts rather than refusing — overlay#323
- [ ] (repo) The format-assertion vocabulary can express structure, seat side first

issues.title: Routine runs with no terminal state (rolling)
issues.body:
Triggered routine runs that ended in no observable terminal state.

Every run is supposed to end delivered, refused with the reason
delivered, or escalated. Anything listed below ended in silence,
which from a client's side is indistinguishable from nothing
having happened (ss#2367) or from nothing having run (ss#2136).

**This issue is rewritten in place on every run.** The counts below
are current as of the run linked at the bottom, not a snapshot of
the day it was opened. A comment is added only when the finding set
changes, so the comment thread is the history of what moved.

issues.title: One condition, one issue: the terminal-state reconciler files a new P1 daily instead of updating the one it already opened
issues.body:
## The defect

`terminal-state-reconcile.yml` files a brand-new `prio:P1` GitHub issue on every scheduled run. Seven issues between 08-18 and 08-24 (#2401, #2438, #2480, #2512, #2545, #2560, #2567), one per day, each a full re-report. Eight were closed as duplicates on 08-24; #2401 remains open.

The obvious fix — de-duplicate by fingerprint and stay silent when the finding set is unchanged — is **wrong here, and was nearly shipped**. The finding set grew on 5 of 6 day-over-day transitions (350 → 361 → 376 → 380 → 388 → 389 → 389). The control is firing for cause; see #2581. A fingerprint dedupe would have suppressed 1 of the 7 and taught everyone to skim the rest.

## What is actually wrong

One condition is occupying one issue per day, so a real change in the number is invisible in a stack of near-identical P1s. The count moving is the information. The fix is to keep the signal and stop multiplying the containers.

## The shape

**One open issue, updated in place.** The reconciler emits a stable `reconcile-series:` marker — constant for this control, *not* a hash of the findings. Before filing, the workflow searches open `prio:P1` issue **bodies** for that marker (bodies, not titles: the title carries the date, which is why no title check could ever have caught the duplicates — see the comment at `unaudited-send-reconcile.yml:166-168`). Found → edit that issue's body with today's counts, and comment only when the totals moved. Not found → file one.

**A finding-set digest decides comment-or-stay-quiet**, and it must be built from stable identities. `Obligation.row_id` is the audit ledger's own primary key (`reconcile-outcomes.py:252`) and is the right primary key, but it is `None` for claimed obligations (`:309-316`), so a second keyspace with a marker prefix is required — the sibling reconciler solves the identical problem at `reconcile-sends.py:753`. The slug must come from the `SeatReport`, never the obligation: the claimed constructor takes `slug=str(claim.get("slug") or "")`, which can be empty and would collide across seats. The key must exclude `rows_read`, `rows_in_window`, `pending` and `routine_class` — the first two are recomputed per window, `pending` depends on `now`, and `routine_class` is mutated in place at `:287`.

**HOLD must stay loud.** `pilot-law` has been unevaluated for seven consecutive days (`HOLD pilot-law: audit_export read failed … Name or service not known` in every one of the seven bodies). The daily P1 is currently the only surface reporting it. Collapsing to one issue therefore has to write HOLD lines into `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on **every** run including the quiet path, or this trades a noisy true report for a silent blind spot — the same failure one layer down.

**No baseline file.** A baseline suppresses *dispositioned* findings. Nothing in the 389 has been dispositioned.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (repo) A stable `reconcile-series:` marker is emitted in `render()` only, never in `--json`, at column 0 so the workflow's `sed -n 's/^…//p'` anchor holds
- [x] (repo) A finding-set digest is built from stable identities; a test mutates only `rows_read` and asserts the digest is unchanged, and a second adds a genuine finding and asserts it changes
- [x] (repo) The workflow updates an existing open issue rather than filing a second, and comments only when the totals moved
- [x] (repo) HOLD lines reach `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on every run, including the run that files and comments nothing
- [ ] (runtime) `workflow_dispatch` twice: the first run leaves exactly one issue, the second files no second issue and its summary names the open one
- [ ] (runtime) The next **scheduled** run on live data updates that issue rather than filing, and if the count moved it says so — this is the row that proves the marker survived real drift, which two dispatches minutes apart cannot show
- [ ] (runtime) Close the issue and dispatch: it re-files. A quieted watchdog that cannot be re-armed is not quieted, it is broken

## Related

- #2581 — the defect this control is correctly reporting
- ss#2388 — the reconciler itself (hardening track 4)
- ss#2386 / ss#2345 — the sibling reconciler's de-duplication, which is the right fix *there* and the wrong one here
- A seat held on N consecutive runs should escalate on its own. `pilot-law` proves the gap; not in this scope

issues.title: pilot-smokeball accrues ~5 new silent routine runs a day, and the daily report of it was nearly muted as noise
issues.body:
## The defect

`pilot-smokeball` accrues new silent routine runs every single day. Measured from the bodies of the seven `Routine run with no terminal state` issues filed 08-18 through 08-24:

| Issue | Date | ashton-price | pilot-smokeball | total silent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #2401 | 08-18 | 0 (`ok`) | 315 | 350 |
| #2438 | 08-19 | 4 | 322 | 361 |
| #2480 | 08-20 | 7 | 334 | 376 |
| #2512 | 08-21 | 7 | 338 | 380 |
| #2545 | 08-22 | 7 | 346 | 388 |
| #2560 | 08-23 | 7 | 347 | 389 |
| #2567 | 08-24 | 7 | 347 | 389 |

`pilot-smokeball` went 315 → 347 in six days, roughly five new silent runs a day. `ashton-price` — the paying client's seat — went 0 → 7 on 08-19/08-20 and has been flat since.

A silent run is one that ended in none of the three terminal states the contract allows (delivered, refused-with-reason-delivered, escalated). From a client's side that is indistinguishable from nothing having happened (ss#2367) or from nothing having run (ss#2136).

## Why this is filed now

The seven issues above were read as noise — a reconciler re-reporting a standing backlog — and a de-duplication fix was designed for them. That diagnosis was wrong, and the table is why: the finding set **grew on 5 of 6 transitions**. The reconciler is not crying wolf. It is correctly reporting a live, growing failure, once a day, and the response was almost to mute it.

The seven issues were the symptom. This is the defect.

## What is not yet known

- **Which routines.** The issue bodies carry per-finding lines (`WEBHOOK_ROUTED [reply_to_person] ended_without_outcome skill=matter-inbox-router`), so the shape is available per row but has not been aggregated.
- **Whether the ~5/day is one recurring routine or a spread.**
- **Whether the `ashton-price` 0 → 7 step on 08-19/08-20 shares a cause** with the pilot trend or is separate.
- **Whether any of these silences reached a person.** That is the question that decides severity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) The daily accrual is attributed: which routines, which shapes, and whether it is one cause or several — aggregated from the audit rows, not from the issue prose
- [ ] (repo) The `ashton-price` 0 → 7 step is explained, since that is the seat a paying client uses
- [ ] (runtime) For at least one accruing routine, the silence is reproduced and its cause named from the seat's own audit ledger, with a `crane_verify` ID
- [ ] (runtime) Either the accrual stops, or it is dispositioned with evidence that no silence reaches a person — and the disposition is recorded where the reconciler can read it, not in prose

## Related

- The reconciler that found this: `operator/bin/reconcile-outcomes.py`, `.github/workflows/terminal-state-reconcile.yml` (ss#2388, hardening track 4)
- `pilot-law` has been unevaluated for all seven days (`HOLD pilot-law: audit_export read failed … Name or service not known`) — a separate gap, filed separately
- Found while measuring the backlog with `scripts/backlog-census.ts` (#2570, #2578)

issues.title: A refused escalation must itself escalate: the pilot's deadline digest was refused by its own gates for four days and nobody was paged
issues.body:
## Sentence

When a pilot-smokeball routine has something that needs a human and its email is refused by a gate (or never attempted), team@smd.services gets a page naming the routine and the reason within minutes; and the deadline escalator's digest, whose dates the pre-run script read from Smokeball, is no longer refused for those dates, so Scott receives it.

**Terminal seams:** (a) an email in team@ from the fleet-alerts Worker; (b) `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED` to scott@ from the escalator's cron turn.

## What happened

Since 08-18 the pilot Operator has had things to tell Scott and could not get them past its own gates. 08-19: the deadline escalator woke with a court date 7 days out, tried `smd_send_message` five times, every attempt refused (identifier gate `date` x4, em-dash marker x1). 08-20: woke with 5 needs-you items and did not try. The same routine was muted 08-04..08-09 by the voice-spec gate (#2234) and on 08-13 by the send-tool TypeError (#2348). Each time the refusal was an audit row on the seat nobody was watching; from outside, "refused", "did not try", and "nothing to report" are identical. Evidence: vfy_01M0N0NZBPQX6XADDVTZ5DEZXP.

Root cause of the date refusals: the escalator's `pre_run.py` reads the authored dates from Smokeball and hands them to the model as prompt text; nothing seeds the provenance register from that output, so the gate sees the dates as composed. A seeding gap, not an over-broad rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (repo) Overlay heartbeat emits `send_refusals`, `send_refusals_last_ts`, `send_refusals_json` over a 24h window covering refused cron sends, `CONFIRM_SEND_FAILED`, and wakes with `digest_needs_you > 0` that dispatched nothing

- [x] (repo) Staff-class sends normalize em/en dashes instead of being refused; client/vendor classes unchanged

- [x] (runtime) Falsifier: a one-shot cron turn whose send is refused produces `send_refusals = 1`, a `last_seen_marker`, and the page in team@; a second beat does not re-page
- [x] (runtime) Handoff fence: a one-shot turn asked to write the handoff file is refused
- [ ] (runtime) Escalator run with `digest_needs_you > 0` dispatches to scott@ with no refusal row of any kind in that session



## Evidence

| AC | Evidence |

| Console ingest + pager | #2548 (c2b94aa4): migrations/0109, heartbeat.ts, workers/fleet-alerts/src/send-refused.ts + tests |
