issues.title: Audit body_digest is independently checkable from the firm's own Sent Items copy
issues.body:
## The sentence

Counsel holding the firm's own Sent Items copy of a disputed email can recompute the digest on the audit row and confirm the body is what left the Operator — **without taking SMD's word for it**.

## What the digest is today

`body_digest = sha256(subject + text + html)` as joined by `relay.draft_body` (`hermes-smd-reply/relay.py:100-125`), an internal string the content and fabrication floors scan. The subject is not even transmitted (a reply threads under "Re:"). The recipe is documented nowhere a client can see. So the digest proves consistency **inside SMD's own system**; an outsider cannot reproduce it from the message they hold.

## Constraint an implementer must know first

The paid seat's replies go through `POST /messages/{id}/reply` with `{"comment": ...}` (`operator/workspace_broker/msgraph_ops.py:416-447`). **Graph composes the stored message** — its own HTML wrapper plus the quoted original. `sha256(comment)` will never equal `sha256(stored body)`. A byte-equality recipe cannot pass on the reply path, by construction, for every A&P send to date.

Two honest shapes:

- **(a) Containment.** Digest over exactly the authored text; the verification recipe is "the authored text appears verbatim in the stored body", with the quoted-original caveat stated. Works on both `sendMail` and `/reply`. **This issue builds (a).**
- **(b) Broker-composed body.** `createReply` → set body → `send`, giving a body SMD controls byte-for-byte. Needs `Mail.ReadWrite` on the send app, which breaks the `Mail.Send`-only two-app fence (`msgraph_ops.py:19-26`, overlay#280). Same Captain decision as #2499; named here as contingent on it, not built.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Send rows carry `body_digest_authored` — sha256 over exactly the authored plain-text bytes handed to Graph / AgentMail — and `body_digest_authored_html` when HTML was authored. The existing scan digest keeps its name and meaning.
- [ ] (repo) The evidence packet README (`operator/adapter/evidence/packet.py` `_readme_text`) and `docs/handbook/security-trust.md` state the recipe: for `sendMail`, byte equality against the stored body; for `/reply`, containment of the authored text in the stored body; with a worked `openssl dgst -sha256` / `grep -F` example.
- [ ] (repo) `src/lib/portal/operator/object-audit-record.ts` CSV exports the new columns.
- [ ] (runtime) One A&P `sendMail` send recomputed from the mailbox copy matches by equality; one `/reply` send verifies by containment. Performed against the pilot's M365 sandbox if the firm's mailbox is not available to SMD. `crane_verify` ids in the PR.

## Non-goals

No canonicalization of HTML — the firm verifies the bytes its mail system stored, and a recipe that normalizes is a recipe that can be argued with.

## Provenance

Audit-fitness assessment 2026-08-20, scenario S4. Priority 5 of 5; follows #2497 through #2500.

issues.title: Audit chain head pinned off the Machine, verified daily, ledger copied off-box daily
issues.body:
## The sentence

A third party — the firm's insurer, the State Bar, opposing counsel, or the firm itself at offboarding — can be shown that the audit record was **not truncated or rewritten by anyone, SMD included**, and that it **survives loss of the Machine**.

## What holds and what does not (falsified, not inferred)

`vfy_01M0H8D1CV2X8J9ZACMAC8E6E2` — `operator/bin/verify-audit-chain.py` run against mutated copies of the live ashton-price export (1,473 rows, baseline INTACT):

| Tamper | Verifier says |
|---|---|
| Mutate a middle row | BROKEN ✅ |
| Delete a middle row | BROKEN ✅ |
| Delete the last 50 rows | **INTACT** |
| Delete the last 1 row | **INTACT** |
| Append a forged row with a valid hash | **INTACT** |
| Mutate a row, re-hash everything after it | **INTACT** |

The chain is unkeyed SHA-256 with a public algorithm (`operator/workspace_broker/chain.py`). The head never leaves the Machine: the heartbeat ships `last_audit_ts` only (`shared/heartbeat.py:75`). `verify-audit-chain.py:11-13` says tail truncation "is caught by comparing the reported head against an externally pinned head" — nothing pins one. And **nothing calls the verifier**: not a workflow, not the evidence packet (`operator/adapter/evidence/packet.py` imports no chain code), not the portal CSV export. It runs when a human runs it.

The only copy of the ledger off the broker's file is Fly's daily volume snapshot, **5-day retention** (`fly volumes snapshots list vol_4y8d71n6dy60063r -a hermes-ashton-price`). No periodic seam pull exists (`seam_pull.py` is pull-before-destroy; the reconcilers pull and discard). The A&P ledger already lost its pre-2026-07-29 rows once when the seat was rebuilt on a new volume.

What the record can honestly claim today: the **agent** cannot alter or erase it (single broker writer, agent uid read-only — `audit_ledger.py:167-207`, no update/delete verb on the IPC surface, `server.py:437-440`). Anyone with root can, undetectably. ADR 0074 watch class 4 is the deferred design for exactly this; its trigger (b) has arguably fired via #2258. Service agreement §4.5: "hash-chained, append-only … kept for the life of the engagement."

## Prior design to dispose of

`docs/specs/operator/audit-log-immutability.md` specifies an R2 mirror + `check_audit_integrity` from the D1/Logpush era (ADR 0023). Either mark it superseded in this PR or adopt its loader interface. Do not leave two designs standing.

Already exists, reuse: `AlertSource` includes `'audit_integrity'` (`src/lib/admin/cost-anomaly.ts:240`, rendered `src/lib/admin/fleet-status.ts:183`, seeded by migration 0044). There is no `watchdog` source; do not invent one. Daily jobs in this repo are GitHub Actions + `operator/bin/lib/seam_pull.py` (`control-probes.yml`, `unaudited-send-reconcile.yml`), not Worker crons (`wrangler.toml` has no triggers). R2 writes use the credential `customer-config-reconcile.yml` uses.

## Honesty line for the docs

A pinned head protects rows **older than the last persisted head**. Rows newer than it remain rewritable by root until the next heartbeat. Persist every heartbeat's head, not a daily sample, and say so in the handbook.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) The heartbeat carries `audit_head` (row_hash of the chain tip) and `audit_rows` — a one-line addition to the existing read-only query at `shared/heartbeat.py:75-100`. The console persists **every** head into an append-only per-seat table (migration).
- [ ] (repo) A daily Actions workflow in the shape of `control-probes.yml` pulls `audit_export` over the seam, runs `verify_chain`, checks the new head **descends** from the last pinned head (the prior head appears as some row's `row_hash` in the export), and writes an `audit_integrity` alert on chain break, head mismatch, or head regression. Tri-state per #2395: a transport failure is a hold and still fails the run.
- [ ] (repo) The same workflow writes the export to R2 under `audit/<slug>/<date>.json.gz` on an immutable / object-locked prefix, and records the object key + sha256 in the run summary.
- [ ] (repo) `verify-audit-chain.py` and the evidence packet accept `--pinned-head` and report tail truncation as a break. The packet README states the pin source.
- [ ] (repo) `docs/handbook/security-trust.md` and `src/pages/security.astro` say what is now true, including the honesty line above.
- [ ] (runtime) Pilot: a deliberate tail-truncation on a copied export is caught by the workflow (the falsifier that failed today passes). A&P: first head pinned, first R2 copy present. Alert fires on a synthetic head mismatch. `crane_verify` ids in the PR.

## Non-goals

No per-row signing. No second Machine per seat. No LLM-in-the-loop watchdog. (ADR 0074's rejected options; nothing in the scenario set needed them beyond what this closes.)

## Provenance

Audit-fitness assessment 2026-08-20, scenario S8. Priority 4 of 5; follows #2497, #2498, #2499.

issues.title: msgraph sends are reconciled against the audit ledger and carry the Sent Items message id
issues.body:
## The sentence

If a message leaves the Operator's mailbox in the firm's Microsoft 365 tenant that the Operator did not send, SMD learns within a day. And every send the Operator did make can be located in the firm's mailbox **by id**.

## What exists today

- `operator/bin/reconcile-sends.py` is AgentMail-only (`AGENTMAIL_API_BASE`, `list_sent` on `/inboxes`). `.github/workflows/unaudited-send-reconcile.yml` runs it daily. It covers **zero** msgraph seats. The paid seat sends through msgraph (service agreement §4.6: AgentMail is not used for this firm).
- Graph answers `sendMail` and `/messages/{id}/reply` with 202 and no body (`operator/workspace_broker/msgraph_ops.py:304, 389, 447`). So every A&P `REPLY_SENT` row carries `sent_message_id: '(sent via msgraph, id unavailable)'` (8/8) and every `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED` row `message_id: ''` (9/9) — `vfy_01M0H8DR6JAPYVHFMNJZXQZ517`.
- The class this detects is real: #2258 found 9 of 121 pilot sends with no audit row (one to a real client address). That control does not exist on the paid seat, and if a foreign send happened there today, the ledger's silence would be read as "the Operator didn't do it" with no instrument behind the claim.

## Dependency

**#2345 (OPEN):** the AgentMail reconciler re-files a fixed historical backlog every day because it has no per-send acknowledgement. The msgraph adapter must land **with** watermark / acknowledgement semantics, or after #2345 closes. Copying today's shape copies the cry-wolf onto the paid seat.

## Exact-match key (decision point)

Matching by subject + time window is a heuristic. The exact key, and the pick here: the broker stamps an `internetMessageHeaders` entry `X-SMD-Audit-Row: <row ulid>` on `sendMail`, and the Sent Items lookup + reconciler key on it.

**Probe first:** whether `/messages/{id}/reply` accepts a `message` object carrying headers alongside `comment`. If Graph refuses headers on `/reply`, the alternative is `createReply` → set body/headers → `send`, which needs `Mail.ReadWrite` on the **send** app and breaks the `Mail.Send`-only two-app fence (`msgraph_ops.py:19-26`, overlay#280). That is the Captain's decision, not this issue's; it is the same decision #ISSUE5 hinges on. Record the probe result on this issue and stop there if it comes up refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `msgraph_ops.send` stamps `X-SMD-Audit-Row`; `msgraph_ops.reply` stamps it or the probe result is recorded on this issue with the Graph response.
- [ ] (repo) After the 202, a bounded Sent Items lookup on the **read** credential (the reply path already holds `conversationId` for free from the sender-verification GET at `msgraph_ops.py:425-431` via `$select`) returns `internetMessageId` + Graph id, and both land on the `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED` and `REPLY_SENT` rows. Lookup failure is recorded on the row (`lookup: failed`), never silently blank.
- [ ] (repo) `reconcile-sends.py` gains an msgraph adapter reading the seat mailbox's Sent Items, read-only and mailbox-scoped (§4.6), matching exact on header / id first, tool-path by window second, with the same tri-state as AgentMail and **with** ack/watermark memory (#2345).
- [ ] (repo) The workflow runs the adapter for every seat whose `customer.yaml` mail adapter is msgraph. Kill test in the shape of `[UNAUDITED-KILLTEST-2258]`, on the pilot's M365 sandbox mailbox, proven to file.
- [ ] (runtime) The daily run on ashton-price reports `sent=N exact=N unaccounted=0` with N>0. The out-of-band-send falsifier runs on the **pilot's M365 sandbox** mailbox (SMD has no UI access to the firm's tenant; the firm is the only UI oracle there) and is reported the next run. `crane_verify` ids in the PR.

## Non-goals

No change to AgentMail reconciliation. No client-visible surface.

## Provenance

Audit-fitness assessment 2026-08-20, scenarios S3 and S4. Priority 3 of 5; follows #2497 (row fields) and #2498.

issues.title: Audit joins: the ledger cannot name the person, the message, or the matter behind an action
issues.body:
## The sentence

A Named Administrator at the firm pulls the audit record for one Operator action and sees **who caused it** (which rostered person, or which routine), **which message it answered**, and **which matter it concerned**.

## What the ledger answers today

Measured on the live ashton-price ledger, 1,473 rows pulled over the read seam 2026-08-21 (`vfy_01M0H8DR6JAPYVHFMNJZXQZ517`), and the pilot (8,913 rows):

| Row class | What it carries | What it lacks |
|---|---|---|
| `INBOUND_RECEIVED` | random `item_id` (`shared/inbound.py:96`, `token_hex`), `content_digest`, `trust_class`, `verification_detail` (e.g. `sender_is_admin`) | any sender identity; the vendor message id |
| `REPLY_SENT` / `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED` / `REPLY_HELD` / `REPLY_FAILED` | recipient, recipient class, body digest, in_reply_to | `session_id` (0/8, 0/9, 0/2, 0/1 on A&P; 0/207, 0/112 on pilot), `matter_ref` (0 everywhere) — `agent_event_params` in `shared/audit_contract.py` takes neither argument |
| `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED` | `matter_id` when the args carried one (`SCOPE_KEYS = ("matter_id","customer_segment")`, `plugins/hermes-smd-audit/schemas.py:321`), tool name, trust trail | document / memo id; any digest of what was read or written; `smd_deliver_draft` rows carry no matter at all |

Of 10 A&P sessions that contained a send, 3 have a `matter_ref` on any row. A reconstructed real trace (the 08-20 22:35Z reply) works only because the rows are seconds apart — the joins are by timestamp adjacency, not by key.

## Why it matters (the scenarios this fails)

- **#2167 (P0, cross-matter leak):** session `20260820_195837_68d654ce` read four distinct matters and then dispatched two sends. The ledger shows the reads and the sends and **cannot say which matter the sends concerned**. Its silence looks like evidence of innocence.
- **Employee misuse:** the ledger can say "a verified admin sent the instruction"; it cannot say which one. Naming the person means opening the mailbox and matching by time and digest.
- **Disputed communication:** a reply row cannot name the matter it was about.

Service agreement §2.2 ("every action is recorded"), §4.5; this is the client-facing half of what the record is sold as.

## Overlap

#2152 (capture the verified replying sender on an ack) is the ack slice of this issue; treat as subsumed and close it against this one's PR if its ACs are met.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `INBOUND_RECEIVED` rows carry `sender_key = sha256(recipient_policy.canonicalize(address))` (`operator/workspace_broker/recipient_policy.py:48` — the NFC+strip+lower primitive; never the raw address; a rostered display name may ride along as a label, never as identity) and the vendor message id (`internetMessageId` / Graph id for msgraph, AgentMail message id for agentmail).
- [ ] (repo) `REPLY_SENT`, `REPLY_HELD`, `REPLY_FAILED`, `CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED`, `CONFIRM_SEND_FAILED` rows carry `session_id` and `matter_ref` whenever the turn resolved one. `agent_event_params` gains both arguments; the writers in `hermes-smd-reply`, `hermes-smd-trust`, and the broker's msgraph/agentmail ops pass them. `matter_ref` lands in the COLUMN, not only metadata.
- [ ] (repo) Read/write tools (`mcp_smokeball_create_memo`, `mcp_smokeball_read_document`, `mcp_smokeball_get_files_on_matter`, `smd_deliver_draft`, msgraph/agentmail `create_draft`) carry the document / memo / draft id and a sha256 of the body written, in metadata. `build_per_tool_metadata`'s docstring lists the new keys; `tests/test_audit_vocabulary_completeness.py` and the contract tests pin them.
- [ ] (repo) No new columns; chain canonicalization is unchanged (metadata is already one of the 12 hashed columns — existing rows keep verifying).
- [ ] (repo) `src/lib/portal/operator/object-audit-record.ts` parses and renders the new fields; the CSV exports them.
- [ ] (runtime) On ashton-price after the pin-bump + reprovision (Captain-gated, separate step), one real inbound → reply trace pulled over the seam shows `sender_key`, vendor message id, `session_id`, and `matter_ref` on the send row. `crane_verify` id in the PR.

## Non-goals

No raw email addresses in any row (exports leave the Machine). No retry/queue for audit writes. No portal Activity feed copy changes.

## Provenance

Audit-fitness assessment 2026-08-20: `vfy_01M0H8D1CV2X8J9ZACMAC8E6E2` (chain falsifier), `vfy_01M0H8DR6JAPYVHFMNJZXQZ517` (A&P ledger structure). Priority 1 of 5.

issues.title: Establishment files templates the renderer will never open: an authored templates: override silently shadows the Template - <Class> convention
issues.body:
## What happened

Proving the #2448 establishment row on pilot-smokeball, the `document-library-establishment` turn filed three class templates and reported:

> The renderer will use them as the base document for any future draft of the matching class.

An independent resolution probe (vfy_01M0GHR4T1V6HG46BVX3S61BCC) shows that is true for exactly one of the three.

```
config templates: {'demand_letter': 'Template - Demand Letter (Policy Limits)',
                   'discovery_response': 'Template - Discovery Responses (RFP and FROG Combined)'}

letter             -> 'Template - Letter'  sha 09eef4b4...  MATCHES what the turn filed
discovery_response -> 'Template - Discovery Responses (RFP and FROG Combined)'  sha 06b8ecbf...
demand_letter      -> 'Template - Demand Letter (Policy Limits)'  sha 45366e01...
```

The two files the turn just created (`Template - Discovery Response`, sha `b9546d80...`; `Template - Demand Letter`, sha `a5d2ef39...`) are inert. Neither sha appears in any resolution.

## Root cause

`library.resolve_template` prefers an authored `self_initiation.document_library.templates[<class>]` over the `Template - <Class>` convention — correctly, that is the override's purpose. But `document-library-establishment` files under the **convention** without consulting the override, so on any seat that authors a mapping the two disagree and the newly filed file is dead on arrival.

Not a resolver bug. The two halves were built against different assumptions about who names the file.

## Why it matters beyond the wasted file

The delivery note asserted the templates were live. An administrator who then edits `Template - Demand Letter.docx` in Word will see no change in any draft, with nothing anywhere reporting why. That is the silent-fallback failure mode the loud `templateExpected` reporting was added to prevent (#2475), reappearing one layer up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Establishment resolves the target file name through the same path the renderer uses, so it files under the authored name when an override exists and under the convention when it does not
- [ ] (repo) When establishment files a template for a class whose authored override names a different file, the delivery note says so explicitly rather than claiming the new file is live
- [ ] (repo) Test: a seat config with an override + an establishment file lands on ONE name, and `resolve_template` returns the bytes that were just filed
- [ ] (runtime) On a seat with an authored override, run establishment for that class and confirm by sha that the renderer resolves to the file the turn filed

## Evidence

| Claim | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Three filed, one live | vfy_01M0GHR4T1V6HG46BVX3S61BCC |
| Establishment turn runs on 0.20.4 (context) | vfy_01M0GHARFS33PSMKZRQZJTQ0PZ |

Refs #2448.

issues.title: Boot-smoke races the provisioner writing /var/lib/smd-config, and the abort hides the 21 checks after it
issues.body:
Hit on hermes-ashton-price — the **paying client's seat** — during the ss#2444 hook-order-fix reprovision at 19:28:54Z.

## What happened

The deploy succeeded. Machine reached `started`, health good, new image `deployment-01M0G9Q5PQRVVKXW6H5DN71AYJ`. Then boot-smoke aborted at check 6 of 27:

```
[19:28:53Z] PASS: customer-yaml-not-agent-writable
[19:28:54Z] FAIL: customer-yaml-dir-not-agent-writable — command failed:
             setpriv --reuid=hermes --regid=hermes --init-groups sh -c "! test -w /var/lib/smd-config"
[19:28:54Z] FATAL: Boot smoke test failed — Machine is up but dependency chain is unhealthy.
```

**The end state is correct.** Probed four minutes later:

```
drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 4096 Aug 20 19:28 /var/lib/smd-config
setpriv --reuid=hermes ... test -w /var/lib/smd-config  ->  not-writable
```

A standalone re-run of the same script: **27/27 PASS**, including the check that failed.

## Why it failed — a race, not a permission bug

Look at the mtimes. `/var/lib/smd-config` and its `specs/` subdirectory are both stamped **19:28** — the same minute the check ran. The provisioner was still materializing `specs/` into that directory when boot-smoke tested whether the directory was agent-writable. The check sampled the window before the final ownership/mode settled.

So the assertion is right, the timing is wrong: it is asserting a *settled* property while the thing is still being written.

## The dangerous half is the abort, not the flake

Check 6 failing meant checks **7 through 27 never ran.** Those include the three that exist specifically to catch a bad promotion:

- `hermes-sha-matches-pin` — is the running Hermes the pinned one
- `matter-mixing-fence` — does the ss#2167 read fence discriminate
- `msgraph-send-credential-stripped-from-agent` — can the agent see the send credential

A timing-sensitive check placed sixth can therefore mask 21 real ones, and the operator sees "FATAL: dependency chain is unhealthy" — which reads like the seat is broken when the seat is fine, and would read identically if the seat were genuinely compromised. **On this run I had to re-run the script by hand to discover the seat was healthy.** Someone under time pressure could equally have rolled back a good deploy, or waved through a bad one on the assumption it was "that flaky check again" — which is the failure this repo has already been bitten by elsewhere (see #2486).

## Fix, in preference order

1. **Make the check wait for settlement rather than sample it.** Poll `! test -w` for a few seconds before failing, the way `machine-state-started` already waits up to 60s. Cheap, local, keeps the assertion.
2. **Have the provisioner finish writing before boot-smoke starts.** The real ordering bug is that boot-smoke begins while `specs/` materialization is in flight. A barrier is the honest fix; the poll above is the belt.
3. **Do not abort the run on the first failure.** Run all 27, report every result, exit non-zero at the end. A gate that stops at the first red hides the state of everything after it, and the whole value of 27 checks is seeing which ones failed together.

(3) is the one I would take first even if (1) and (2) never happen: it converts a misleading FATAL into a complete picture.

## Falsifier

Reprovision a seat and, with no fix, watch check 6 fail on a run where `specs/` is being written; with the fix, the same run must reach check 27. A fix that merely makes the race rarer has not fixed it — verify by artificially delaying the `specs/` write and confirming the check still passes.

Refs #2444, #2486

issues.title: Flaky merge gate: test_list_all_returns_every_job_newest_first assumes ULIDs from the same millisecond sort by creation order
issues.body:
`substrate` failed on PR #2484 with a failure that has nothing to do with that PR (its diff touches five files, zero of them under `workspace_broker/`). It passed on re-run. Filing rather than just re-running, because **a flaky merge gate is worse than a slow one**: it teaches everyone to hit re-run without reading, which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through.

## The failure

`operator/workspace_broker/tests/test_job_ledger.py::test_list_all_returns_every_job_newest_first`

```
assert ids == sorted(ids, reverse=True)
E  At index 1 diff: '01M0G8FZCR2Z4EAQPQQCZW4G2J' != '01M0G8FZCRKQSS3RN2S53CDE0V'

  returned: ['01M0G8FZCSR7WK1WCS1FYG1CN3', '01M0G8FZCR2Z4EAQPQQCZW4G2J', '01M0G8FZCRKQSS3RN2S53CDE0V']
  expected: ['01M0G8FZCSR7WK1WCS1FYG1CN3', '01M0G8FZCRKQSS3RN2S53CDE0V', '01M0G8FZCR2Z4EAQPQQCZW4G2J']
```

## Why it flakes

Look at the three ULIDs. They share the prefix `01M0G8FZC` — **all three were minted inside the same millisecond.** The test creates them back to back with no clock control:

```python
first  = _new_job(w)
second = _new_job(w)
third  = _new_job(w)
```

The assertion's own comment says *"ULIDs are lexicographically time-sortable"*. That is true **across** milliseconds and false **within** one: inside a single millisecond the remaining 80 bits are random, so the lexicographic order of same-millisecond ULIDs is a coin flip. The test therefore asserts a property the data structure does not have, and passes only when the random suffixes happen to land in the right order.

It is a real assertion about a real seam — `list_all()` must return newest-created first for the `jobs` runtime-read kind — but it is currently testing the random suffix, not the ordering.

## Fix options, in preference order

1. **Control the clock.** Mint the three jobs at distinct, explicit timestamps the way the rest of this file already does with `T0`. Then the ULID prefixes differ, the ordering is deterministic, and the test asserts the property it claims to.
2. **Assert against creation order, not sortedness.** `assert ids == [third, second, first]` states the actual contract ("newest-created first") and cannot pass by luck.

Option 2 is stronger: `ids == sorted(ids, reverse=True)` is satisfiable by an implementation that sorts by id rather than by creation time, so it would not catch a regression that swapped those two. Option 1 plus option 2 together is the real fix.

## Falsifier for whoever takes it

Run the fixed test 200 times in a loop. The current one fails a meaningful fraction of the time on a fast machine; the fixed one must be 200/200. If it passes 200/200 *before* the fix too, the flake reproduces only under CI's timing and the loop needs to mint jobs with no sleep between them.

Found while merging #2484 (ss#2444 overlay pin bump).

issues.title: Hermes v0.20.4 hook-order flip: three more post_tool_call consumers are at risk, one of them the audit digest
issues.body:
Spun out of ss#2444 / overlay#287. **This is an unprobed hypothesis with a proven premise, not a finding.** It is filed so it cannot be lost, and it should be closed by evidence in either direction.

## The proven part

Hermes v0.20.4 inverted two hooks. Observed on hermes-ashton-price, same seat, same log, five consecutive tool calls (`vfy_01M0G7DYTBHAGDRQYXX02DKMZJ`):

```
v0.18     pre_tool_call -> post_tool_call        -> transform_tool_result
v0.20.4   pre_tool_call -> transform_tool_result -> post_tool_call
```

`hermes-smd-inbound` applies the quarantine fence at `transform_tool_result`. So on v0.20.4 **every `on_post_tool_call` consumer receives the fenced string where it used to receive the connector's raw text.** That was proven on `hermes-smd-establishment`, which threw `JSONDecodeError` at char 1 on 100% of document reads and is fixed in overlay#287.

## The unprobed part

Six other overlay plugins implement `on_post_tool_call`. Three consume `kwargs["result"]` the same way and have **not** been probed:

| consumer | site | what a fence-instead-of-payload would do |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes-smd-audit` | `__init__.py:117` -> `emit_tool_event(result=kwargs.get("result"))` | **the concerning one.** Feeds `output_digest` on every `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED` row. If the digest now covers the fence wrapper rather than the payload, the audit ledger records a digest of the envelope. Silent, no error, no log line. |
| `hermes-smd-reply` | `relay.py:180` `json.loads(result)`, plus `__init__.py:383/:769` | same parse shape that broke establishment. The A&P round-trip worked end to end after promotion, so this is not fatally broken — but that path was Microsoft mail, not a connector read. |
| `hermes-smd-trust` | `__init__.py:348/:359` | consumes the result when resolving a trust decision. Trust decisions logged normally post-promotion, so no visible break. |

## Why the audit one is worth real attention

Two independent reasons, and the second is the one that would bite:

1. **A digest over the wrapper is not a digest over the content.** The fence embeds a fresh unguessable nonce per item, so the same document read twice produces two different digests. Any downstream that treats `output_digest` as content-addressable — dedup, tamper-evidence, "did this change since last time" — silently stops working.
2. **It is provenance on a client ledger.** Raised by the audit session working the Robertus chronology: the seat's `audit_log` currently understates what the Operator read (that part is the establishment defect). If the digest is also wrong, then reconstructing "what did the Operator look at, and was it the same bytes" from that ledger is doubly unreliable for every row written on A&P since 2026-08-20T17:09Z.

## How to close this

Per consumer, not as a sweep. For each, one probe on a promoted seat that shows what the consumer actually received, and either a fix + falsifier in the shape of overlay#287, or a recorded negative result saying it is unaffected and why.

For the audit digest specifically, the decisive probe is cheap: read one document on a promoted seat, then compare that row's `output_digest` against a digest computed over the connector payload and over the fenced string. Whichever it matches is the answer. If it matches the fence, the rows written on ashton-price since 17:09Z on 2026-08-20 need to be marked as digest-unreliable rather than silently left.

## Deliberately not swept into overlay#287

Establishment had a proven live break with a reproduced traceback. These three have a proven *premise* and no observation. Fixing them on the strength of the premise would have shipped three unfalsifiable changes alongside one real one — see `feedback_check_must_be_able_to_fail`.

Refs #2444

issues.title: A seat cannot say which ss-console commit built it (Hermes and overlay are pinned and asserted; the repo half is not)
issues.body:
A seat records which **Hermes** it runs (`/opt/hermes/HERMES_SHA`, now asserted at boot by the `hermes-sha-matches-pin` step added in #2453) and which **overlay** it runs (`ENV SMD_OVERLAY_REF` + `/app/OVERLAY_REF`, surfaced in the heartbeat `version` field). It records **nothing** about which `ss-console` commit built the rest of the image — the adapter, the skills, the connectors, `bootstrap.sh`, the probes.

Verified on hermes-smd 2026-08-20: `/app/` carries `adapter/`, `skills/`, `connectors/`, `bootstrap.sh`, `overlay-pack/`, the probe scripts — and no build-ref file of any kind.

## What is already guarded (so this issue is narrow)

`operator/bin/provision-customer.sh:189-201` fetches origin at build time and **dies** when the invoking checkout is *behind* `origin/main`, naming the consequence exactly: "Whatever landed in those commits will NOT be in this image." Only `SS_ALLOW_DIVERGENT_SOURCE=1` gets past it, and that logs a bypass BY REQUEST. That guard fired three times during the #2444 rollout and did its job each time.

So the failure mode "a stale checkout silently ships a seat missing someone's merged work" **does not exist**. Do not file it again.

## What is not guarded

The guard covers *behind*, not *diverged*. A branch with its own commits is not behind `origin/main`, so it passes — deliberately, because that is exactly how a staged promotion works (#2444 reprovisioned four seats from an unmerged PR branch by design).

The consequence is not a bad build; it is an **unanswerable question afterwards**. Given a running seat, there is no way to determine which repo state produced it. Concretely, during #2444:

- pilot-smokeball was rebuilt ~8 times across three different branch commits plus a rollback to an older image.
- Three sessions merged work to `main` in the same window, each reasonably asking "is my code on the seat?"
- The only available answers were inference from timestamps and from what each session remembered doing.

`hermes-sha-matches-pin` closes exactly this question for the Hermes version and nothing else. The same shape closes it for the repo.

## What closes this

1. Bake the invoking checkout's identity into the image: pass `SS_BUILD_REF` (HEAD sha) and a dirty/branch marker as build args from `provision-customer.sh`, write them to `/app/BUILD_REF`, and expose as `ENV SS_BUILD_REF` — mirroring how `OVERLAY_REF` is already handled.
2. Add a boot-smoke step asserting `/app/BUILD_REF` equals the invoking checkout's HEAD, so a stale *image* (a seat that was never rebuilt after a merge) is caught the same way a stale Hermes pin now is.
3. Consider surfacing it on the heartbeat next to the overlay `version`, so the fleet view answers "what is each seat built from" without an ssh.

Worth deciding while implementing: a promotion legitimately builds from a branch, so the boot-smoke assertion must compare against the *invoking checkout*, not against `origin/main` — otherwise it fails every staged rollout and gets bypassed, which is worse than not having it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `SS_BUILD_REF` baked into the image and written to `/app/BUILD_REF`
- [ ] (runtime) A promoted seat reports the commit it was built from, verified by ssh
- [ ] (repo) boot-smoke asserts the running image's build ref matches the invoking checkout, and the assertion is proven able to FAIL (build from ref A, assert against ref B)
- [ ] (runtime) The check runs green on a real reprovision

Found during #2444 (Hermes v0.18.0 → v0.20.4 promotion); the `hermes-sha-matches-pin` step there is the template.

issues.title: smd-staging has no vendor-enforced send fence: sandbox MSGRAPH_SEND_* app registration missing
issues.body:
Found while promoting the fleet to Hermes v0.20.4 (#2444). **Pre-existing and unrelated to that upgrade** — the promotion just tried to reprovision the seat and the gate refused.

## What is true now

`operator/bin/reprovision-staging.sh` dies before any build:

> FATAL: msgraph seat smd-staging has no SEND app credential. ... Stage MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_ID__SMD_STAGING and MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_SECRET__SMD_STAGING in the operator env, then re-run.

- Infisical `/ss` prod holds `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_ID__ASHTON_PRICE` and `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_SECRET__ASHTON_PRICE`. It does **not** hold the `__SMD_STAGING` pair (checked with and without imports).
- On the Machine, `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_SECRET` and `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET` have the **same digest** — the old single-app fallback that #2437 removed as a defect.

Evidence: `vfy_01M0DWJMC0RNS9ZYR3Y907AJVY`.

## Why it matters

The two-app split is what gives the msgraph channel a vendor-enforced fence: a read-only registration for the agent, a send-capable one only the broker sees (Captain decision 2026-08-13, ADR 0078). While the sandbox seat runs one app for both, **the sandbox has no fence** — so it is not a faithful rehearsal surface for the behaviour the fence protects, and it cannot be reprovisioned at all.

## What closes this

1. A second Azure app registration in the **sandbox** tenant (Mail.Send only), pinned to `operator@smdopslab.onmicrosoft.com` by an Exchange ApplicationAccessPolicy — same shape as A&P's. Captain lane: see `docs/runbooks/operator/ms-graph-azure-ad-setup.md`.
2. Stage `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_ID__SMD_STAGING` + `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_SECRET__SMD_STAGING` in Infisical `/ss` prod (`crane_secret_set`, values never in a transcript).
3. Reprovision smd-staging (it also promotes it to v0.20.4, which #2444 deferred) and re-run the 2026-08-13 fence proof: the read app is refused sendMail 403 while the broker's send app returns 202.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (runtime) The sandbox tenant has a send-only app registration pinned by ApplicationAccessPolicy
- [ ] (runtime) `MSGRAPH_SEND_CLIENT_ID__SMD_STAGING` / `_SECRET__SMD_STAGING` present in Infisical /ss prod and **distinct** from the read app's values
- [ ] (runtime) smd-staging reprovisions cleanly and boot-smoke passes, including `hermes-sha-matches-pin`
- [ ] (runtime) Fence proven on the sandbox seat: read app 403 on sendMail, broker send app 202.
2. Overlay tests driving a bridge call through  and the trust gate.
3. Flip the pin to  on pilot-smokeball only, run a rehearsal card command that needs Smokeball, and confirm: the turn still completes, no refused-unmapped rows, and the first-call token count drops.
4. Only then flip the fleet default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Bridge tools classified with tests (overlay)
- [ ] (runtime)  on pilot-smokeball with a rehearsal turn completing and zero unmapped refusals
- [ ] (runtime) First-call token count measured before/after on the same command
- [ ] (repo) Fleet default flipped only after the above
EOF
)

issues.title: smokeball connector: .msg files (the majority file type on real matters) have no extraction path and hard-refuse the docx draft lane
issues.body:
## Observed (Robertus 201923 census, 2026-08-19, vfy_01M0E7J83943K8KKXRDZC5VHH7)

159 of 271 files on the matter are Outlook .msg files, and extract.py has no extraction path for them: every one is invisible to read_document and to every document-reading skill. On this firm's book that is the MAJORITY file type on a matter (discovery arrives by email, F-012), and records or key correspondence filed as .msg never reach a chronology, deficiency review, or record check.

Consequence already live: _collect_matter_sources marks them unextractable, and record_check refuses EVERY render_docx_draft on a matter carrying any .msg file (record_check.py:141, source_unextractable). On realistic A&P matters the .docx draft path can never pass until .msg is either extractable or excluded by policy from the record check.

## Ask

1. .msg extraction path (extract-msg or oxmsg are pure-python; body text + attachment names at minimum, attachment recursion as a follow-on).
2. Decide the record-check posture for container/email types explicitly (extract vs excluded-by-class), instead of the current implicit refuse-everything.

## Context

Same census as the OCR issue; cross-ref ss#2439 (memo gate). Together these three are what stands between the chronology routine and its authored auto-handle tier on real matters.

issues.title: smokeball connector: no OCR path — scanned records are invisible to every document-reading skill
issues.body:
## Observed (Robertus 201923 census, 2026-08-19, vfy_01M0E7J83943K8KKXRDZC5VHH7)

pypdf-only extraction: 24 of 104 PDFs on the matter (124 pages) have no text layer and yield zero text. The unreadable set is small by pages but clinically dense: Advantage MRI reports (cervical/lumbar/shoulder + right knee), Revolution Ortho report, NPIC office notes, NFB session notes, X-rays, UMI thoracic report, referrals. The bills for these providers all extract; the findings do not.

Also: read_document returns total_chars: 0 for a scanned PDF with NO error (server.py ~1324). It fails quiet. A skill cannot distinguish an empty document from an unreadable one without checking total_chars itself.

## Ask

1. OCR fallback in extract.py when the text layer yields ~nothing (tesseract or vendor OCR; weigh on-seat cost, the seat is 1 vCPU / 1 GB).
2. read_document should mark no-text-layer PDFs explicitly (e.g. extraction: none_scanned) so fail-closed skills can surface them per anti-fiction rules.

## Context

Med-chron rush request for A&P (Christa 2026-08-19). The chronology shipped with the 19 files listed as could-not-read; OCR closes the gap. Cross-ref ss#2439.

## Reachability contract (/wired, 2026-08-19)

**Sentence.** The Operator, put to work on a matter whose records include scanned documents (Robertus 201923 is the live case), reads their content: a chronology or review covers the scanned MRI reports and office notes as cited entries instead of listing them under "could not read". Observed by the Captain driving for Christa (the firm fence keeps client delivery Captain-fronted today).

**Terminal seam.** `read_document` / `_collect_matter_sources` inside the RUNNING smokeball-connector process on `hermes-ashton-price`, returning text for a no-text-layer PDF.

**Probes run before planning (2026-08-19):**
- Connector process env carries NO `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (names-only probe of /proc/<pid>/environ on the seat); the Hermes runtime process holds it. Env is an explicit whitelist: `McpConnectorSpec.env_secrets` in overlay `bootstrap/mcp_registry.py` (smokeball entry ~line 212).
- ss#2453 (Hermes v0.20 promotion) is OPEN (9 checks green, 1 skipped) — the reprovision freeze holds; gates 1-2 below are time-gated behind it plus the Captain's A&P reprovision go.
- Key decision (Captain cost lane, decided this session): REUSE the seat's existing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — vision reads bill to the seat's existing cost plane. Staged as an OPTIONAL env row: a seat without it fail-safes to pypdf-only with explicit unreadable marking.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) extract.py falls back to a Claude vision read when the text layer yields ~nothing; result carries an explicit extraction marker (`pypdf` | `vision` | `none_scanned`), never a silent empty string
- [ ] (repo) read_document response marks the extraction path; a scanned PDF with no credential or over the page cap returns an explicit needs-human-read marker, never total_chars: 0 with no error
- [ ] (repo) vision reads are cached on disk keyed by fileId+sizeBytes so record_check's per-render re-extraction does not re-bill; cache hit proven by test
- [ ] (repo) cost/latency guard: vision only for files at/below the page cap; over-cap files surface explicitly
- [ ] (repo) tests include a mutation falsifier: with the fallback disabled, a scanned fixture returns the explicit unreadable marker (the test can fail)
- [ ] (repo, overlay) registry `env_secrets_optional` row delivers the key to the connector process; consumes contract updated
- [ ] (runtime) connector process env on the reprovisioned seat carries the key (names-only probe) — BLOCKED until ss#2453 merges + Captain A&P reprovision go
- [ ] (runtime) `read_document` on a known scanned file (Adv MRI Report, Robertus 201923) returns the report text with `extraction: vision`, crane_verify ID in Evidence — BLOCKED same
- [ ] (runtime) a chronology-style read over Robertus covers previously-unreadable files as cited content — BLOCKED same

issues.title: The Smokeball cross-matter write guard cannot fire at A&P: 0 of 165 real matter numbers match its regex
issues.body:
## What is wrong

`_verify_matter_reference` (`operator/connectors/smokeball/smokeball_connector/server.py:686-712`) refuses a write whose text cites a matter number other than the one it is filed on. It is called by `create_memo` (`:1860`), `create_task`, `create_event` and the document writes. The comment on it names the stakes plainly: "A memo, task, or event naming a matter other than the one it is filed on is how one matter's facts reach another matter's record."

It extracts cited numbers with `_MATTER_NUMBER_RE` (`:614`):

```python
_MATTER_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:\d{4}-[A-Z]{2}-\d{3,4}|[A-Z]{2}-\d{4}-\d{4})\b")
```

**Ashton & Price's matter numbers are bare digits** — `201537`, `201514`, `200956`, `4853`. None of them match. And when the cited set comes back empty the function returns early ("nothing claims a matter; nothing to verify, and no read to spend"), so **every write to an A&P matter passes the guard unconditionally, and has since the production connect.**

Measured against the 165 real Pending matter numbers: **0 match.** The pilot's synthetic `2026-PI-101` format matches, which is why the guard looks healthy everywhere we test it.

Verify: `vfy_01M0DXHAR1TJDPW73WKBWYC102`

## Why it matters

This is a control that cannot fire for the live client — the Law 12 shape. It is adjacent to P0 #2167 (outbound matter identity) and shares its failure mode: content from one matter reaching another matter's record. Here the exposure is the firm's own file, not an outbound recipient, but the same class.

It also means the pilot proves this guard and the client does not have it. Any confidence we have in the write path is confidence in a tenant whose numbering happens to fit our regex.

## What it is not

Not a fabrication defect and not an incident: there is no evidence of a mis-filed write. This is a dormant control, found by measuring the regex against the client's real data rather than by a failure.

## Fix shape (not prescribing)

The number format is per-tenant, so a hardcoded pattern cannot be right. Options worth weighing: derive the pattern from the tenant's own observed matter numbers; match against the specific numbers read this turn rather than a shape; or resolve candidate tokens through the matter-ref cache the connector already maintains. Whichever it is, the guard should be able to report that it evaluated something — a control that returns early on an empty match set is indistinguishable from one that ran and found nothing wrong.

Found while probing the register's delivery path for #2455.

issues.title: Settlement Closeout: the Operator carries the settled-undistributed workstream (obligation ledger + provider-consolidated chase + register)
issues.body:
## The act (reachability contract, /wired 2026-08-19, critiqued x4)

**Sentence:** Christa (office manager, Named Administrator) asks the Operator where the Pending money stands and receives a current register of every settled-undistributed matter, ranked by age and recorded exposure, with each provider obligation's status — and thereafter, without asking again, a provider whose obligations have gone quiet past the firm's authored threshold produces one consolidated follow-up naming every affected matter, in front of the person who owns it.

**Terminal seam reached by this scope:** the register and the follow-up on `pilot-smokeball`, against a seeded tenant. This earns **Built + Wired-on-pilot**, not Tested-as-client. A&P turn-on is a separate act behind three accepted dependencies (the `@ashtonandprice.com` fence, #2367, crons).

**Why:** letter 27 (2026-08-18) named the 165 Pending matters the firm's #1 job and "the main reason we brought the Operator in" — settled cases whose client money sits undistributed in trust because provider bills are un-negotiated, a California State Bar exposure. SMD answered the master-list half by hand (letter 28) with a throwaway script run by an engineer. This makes the Operator carry the workstream.

**Product feature for any Operator customer**, not an A&P implementation: firm-specific values are authored config, and the trust ledger is a stated contract with no adapter written until we have seen a real export. Proving seat: `pilot-smokeball`.

Plan: `~/.claude/plans/serene-percolating-mist.md`.

## Shape

No new skill. Two extensions:

- **`lien-ledger-tracker`** becomes the obligation ledger — gains the settlement layout as a source, graduates to a stateful `pre_run.py`, and widens from statutory lienholders to every obligation blocking disbursement (76% of the outstanding balance has no lien asserted).
- **`matter-status-digest`** gains the settled-undistributed register section.

The obligation is `(matter, provider)`; the **chase consolidates by provider** with a hard per-provider outreach cap, so a payer appearing on many matters gets one letter rather than one per matter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `lien-ledger-tracker` reads the per-plaintiff settlement layout (`PersonalInjurySettlementDetailsItem`, grouped by `parentIndex`) without flattening; `Providers[]` and `OtherLiensAndBalances[]` both parsed
- [ ] (repo) Obligation identity: `source_id` is the raw provider string casefold + whitespace-collapse only, `authored_date` pinned `None`, plaintiff index carried as an attribute; explicit migration writes `resolved` on the old key and carries the attempt count forward when a name is corrected
- [ ] (repo) Bespoke `pre_run.py` pulls through the connector venv subprocess (no MCP tool, no overlay change); own timeout; exhausted budget yields a partial work list with a coverage count, never a raised run
- [ ] (repo) Provider rollup: one chase per provider per cadence naming every affected matter, hard outreach cap, per-obligation duplicates suppressed
- [ ] (repo) Every chase / stall / resolution writes a one-line internal memo on **its own** matter (single-matter, so the cross-matter write guard is untouched)
- [ ] (repo) Stall sentinels are matter-level; a stall raise never changes a chase attempt count
- [ ] (repo) Register section states its ranking rule, coverage counts, per-matter freshness, and a separate labeled band for status-only matters lacking a corroborating signal
- [ ] (repo) Unauthored `trigger_status` refuses and re-surfaces on the ledger window; unauthored `stall_days` degrades with a header line and keeps tracking
- [ ] (repo) Scale proofs through `httpx.MockTransport`: a 500-row page asserts the truncation fail-open fires and is stated; a >40-distinct-contact page asserts the caption-coverage count is reported non-zero
- [ ] (runtime) Read-back reconciliation: every seeded obligation matches the authored seed, per-field
- [ ] (runtime) The gate emits a work list carrying `attempt` / `last_chased` / `days_quiet` from ledger state, and the per-plaintiff layout is not flattened
- [ ] (runtime) A provider spanning two seeded matters produces exactly one chase naming both
- [ ] (runtime) A fresh ledger reconstructs history from the per-matter memos
- [ ] (runtime) The register renders readably in a message body with no attachment
- [ ] (runtime) A corrected provider name resolves the old key and carries the attempt count forward

## Out of scope, filed separately

Document reconstruction for the 102 matters with no structured provider detail (Captain ruling: next, own contract). Attachment support in `msgraph-mail`. The trust-ledger adapter, pending a real export. The `get_matter_layouts` MCP tool and its overlay coordination — needed only for the interactive "ask right now" path, not the scheduled register.

## Evidence

| Claim | Verify |
| --- | --- |
| `layouts/read` granted, `layouts/write` NOT; pilot tenant has zero Pending and empty layouts | `vfy_01M0DVZGZVTHN6G911NZFP136A` |
| The msgraph-mail connector has no attachment support under any spelling | `vfy_01M0DVZ8GXMHST9GWSSTNSDEAZ` |
| Provider-data coverage is inversely correlated with matter age (0% pre-2010 → 90% 2025+) | `vfy_01M0DWRAEKK3C7AVAV5QP9C32S` |
| The cron pre_run reads Smokeball below the MCP tool layer | `vfy_01M0DXM3DNCMVMB89NEJW1PWRS` |

issues.title: Operator drafts are send-ready in the firm's own format: the renderer fills the firm's Word template (#2068 family, gate chain)
issues.body:
## The act (reachability contract, /wired 2026-08-19, critiqued x3)

**Sentence:** a rostered attorney emails the Operator "draft the [demand / discovery set / mediation brief / memo] on matter X"; they open the filed document from the matter in Word and find it in the firm's own format (template/letterhead, font, spacing, item labels, caption, signature block, proof of service) so that after resolving the reserved-judgment markers nothing needs re-typesetting.

**Terminal seam:** the `.docx` bytes on the matter in the firm's Smokeball, opened in Word. Attachment-on-reply (#2068's other half) and the pointer-note hold (#2367) are separate contracts.

**Principle (ADR 0083 §3):** code owns typography and required elements; the model fills content into structure. Typography lives ONLY in the firm's Word template in its Document Library (a style edited in Word takes effect on the next draft); the tool resolves that template deterministically (the model never picks one); the renderer adds no text, no count, no declaration. Two provenances, equally: the firm's own template/letterhead file, or a starter the Operator files for the firm to edit.

Product feature for any Operator customer. Proving seat: pilot-smokeball. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/luminous-humming-origami.md` (rev 2).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Renderer: `render_docx_draft` / `render_docx_template` accept `document_class`; content renders INTO the firm's template (headers/footers/letterhead, page setup, styles survive; body cleared), named-style contract honored with inline fallbacks reported; class absent = stock render byte for byte; multi-section base refused
- [ ] (repo) Deterministic library resolution from the seat's live customer.yaml (`self_initiation.document_library.{matter_number, folder_name, templates}`) -> matter -> folder -> `Template - <Class>.docx`; "not resolved" is reported (`templateExpected`), never silent
- [ ] (repo) Record-check hygiene: library templates excluded from sources; `.dotx` extracts
- [ ] (repo) Grammar documented once (drafting-discipline Part IV) and carried in the tool descriptions; the model writes labels/numerals/caption/signature/POS as content; the renderer styles only
- [ ] (runtime) Build installed on the proving seat (reprovision); connector uid + tool surface confirmed
- [ ] (runtime) A class-rendered draft filed on a rehearsal matter, downloaded, and opened in Word by a person in the starter format (TNR 12, labels, item text, caption table, page numbers)
- [ ] (repo) All five drafters deliver through `render_docx_draft` with `document_class` and state `formatApplied` in the delivery note; skeleton touch-ups
- [ ] (runtime) Email-driven drafting request from a rostered sender on the proving seat files a class-rendered draft (row 8 by proxy: SMD admin)
- [ ] (repo) Establishment files class starters into the library (`render_docx_template` with `document_class`); `matter_number`/`templates` fields authored + validated; ADR 0083 append; handbook line
- [ ] (runtime) Provenance (b): a starter filed into the pilot library, a style edited in Word and re-uploaded, the next draft honors it
- [ ] (runtime) Provenance (a): a real Word-authored letterhead file placed in the pilot library as `Template - Letter.docx`; a letter-class draft renders into it (header image, margins, firm styles survive), opened in Word

Probes before PR 2: unextractable-document count on a realistic pilot matter (the record check, not the renderer, may be the top gate). Probes at the seat step: whether the Smokeball file listing carries `folderId` and lists subfolder files.

Follow-ups filed separately: `run_record_check` never passes `--propounded` / `--sprog-lint` (gates 7/8 unwired through the render tool); #2068 split into render half (this) and attachment half.

issues.title: medical-chronology-maintainer: memo format collides with the memo content gate — the write can never land at its authored tier
issues.body:
## Observed (SMD batch Lane 2.3, hermes-ashton-price, 2026-08-19, first production run)

The skill ran cleanly on a real matter (10006, first chronology build): exemplary quote discipline (per-entry source citations, extraction limits declared, demand-letter summaries distinguished from chart quotes), and exemplary failure honesty — three memo write attempts were refused by the memo content gate and the skill surfaced that with a confirming get_memos_on_matter read (7 memos, unchanged) instead of asserting success.

**Gate refusal reasons (from the run output):** specific dollar amounts from records read; legal-citation pattern matches on medical procedure codes; a date identifier not traceable.

## The defect

The control is correct (unverifiable amounts/identifiers must not land in the firm's system of record). The SKILL's memo format is what cannot pass it: a chronology quoting superbills inherently carries amounts and procedure codes. At its authored tier (auto-handle, internal record only) the routine's whole point is the memo landing — so as authored today the routine can NEVER complete on a real matter.

## Fix shape

Skill-prose refinement: the memo body references amounts/codes by source pointer ("per-line amounts: see <document>") instead of restating them — the run output already converged on this style for its later entries and proposed exactly this fix itself. Acceptance: a chronology memo lands on a real matter through the gate, and the quoted-entry discipline is preserved in the memo body.

Evidence: seat cron 84c7ba00dee6 output; Lane 2.3 verify (ledger). Cross-ref ss#2258 SMD batch.

issues.title: correction_capture accepted a rule-install from a rostered non-admin once the framing changed — admin status must be enforced server-side, not by model judgment
issues.body:
Found by the shadow firm during the ss#2416 iteration-4 proof (run `shadow-pilot-smokeball-20260818T210927Z-8499256-2a47e3a7825a-notgreen`, 2026-08-18).

When the dispatched email prompt told the seat to fulfil requests ("SENDER STATUS... fulfil it now") for any rostered sender — an iteration-4 wording error, being fixed under ss#2416 — the seat installed a standing rule for **ss-probe-runner**, a reply-authorized sender who is NOT on `scope.admins`. A `CORRECTION_PROPOSED` row was written for the unauthored leg. On the three prior runs the same ask was refused.

The lesson is not the wording error (tracked on ss#2416). It is that **the only thing standing between a non-admin and a rule-install was model judgment**: once one framing sentence changed, the effect fired. The audit provenance-audit thesis applies verbatim — a control that is passing by disposition is not a control. Gate 3 (ss#2222) proved initiation authority with kill tests, but the correction-capture surface evidently accepts the model's word for who is asking.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `correction_capture` (and any sibling standing-rule/config-write tool) enforces the requester's admin status SERVER-SIDE, from the verified inbound origin, never from model-supplied arguments or framing
- [ ] (repo) Kill-test pair: a rostered non-admin's rule-install attempt is refused by the tool with an audit row naming the refusal, and an admin's identical attempt succeeds (Law 12 control)
- [ ] (runtime) Both directions observed on the rig with crane_verify ids; the shadow-firm unauthored-sender scenario keeps this pinned forever after

Related: ss#2416 (framing fix), ss#2222 / Gate 3, Decision #55, ADR 0085 §2 (operator-admin allow list).

issues.title: A&P prod tenant realities: empty roles endpoint, /stagesets IAM deny, file-volume paging, leads axis
issues.body:
## Source

Production Smokeball recon 2026-08-18 (read-only, engagements PR #30, evidence vfy_01M0BABMEKZ77YPRM4DA6333RS). Four runtime facts from the live A&P tenant that the 9-matter staging world never showed; each can silently degrade a routine.

## Findings

1. **`GET /matters/{id}/roles` returns empty on every sampled matter (50/50).** Party data lives inline (`clientIds`/`clients`/`otherSideIds`). Caption composition already reads inline fields (safe), but `get_roles_on_matter` and `get_relationships_on_matter` (nested under roles) return nothing on this tenant. Audit skill paths for roles dependency; add inline-parties fallback or remove.
2. **`GET /stagesets` is IAM-denied on production** (explicit-deny execute-api:Invoke) while `/stages` returns 200 and the `stages/read` scope is granted. Same denial class Smokeball fixed for staging writes on 2026-07-05 by re-promoting the app. If stage definitions are ever needed, this is a vendor ask (ticket thread 617858 / Derek); nothing in the day-one grid appears to need them.
3. **File volume breaks single-page reads**: open-matter files p50 252, p90 2,338, max 31,898 (YoCierge auto-uploads). `get_files_on_matter` default Limit=500 silently truncates on 10%+ of matters. Any consumer of file listings must page or explicitly bound, and say which it does.
4. **Leads are a separate axis** (21 open leads on the tenant; `IsLead` filter). No grid routine addresses leads — make them explicitly out of scope in the sweeps so intake activity cannot leak into matter routines.

## AC
- [ ] roles-dependency audit across skills + fallback decision
- [ ] file-listing consumers page or bound explicitly
- [ ] sweeps fence to IsLead=false
- [ ] stagesets dependency confirmed absent (or vendor ask filed)

issues.title: Smokeball connector: SMOKEBALL_REGION never staged + unconsumed env_static declaration
issues.body:
## Why

Found during the 403 sweep (wiring audit, 2026-08-18). Neither caused the A&P incident; both are silent-wrong-behavior traps for future seats.

## What

1. `operator/bin/provision-customer.sh:883-906` stages CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/API_KEY/ENVIRONMENT (+conditional AUTH_MODE/ACCOUNT_ID) but never SMOKEBALL_REGION; `client.py:596` defaults region to "us". Correct for US firms, silently wrong gateway for any future AU/UK firm — and the API key is region-scoped (six distinct keys on six gateways in three AWS regions), so the failure would be a confusing 403, exactly the class we just spent days on. Stage region from customer.yaml with an explicit default.
2. `operator/connectors/smokeball/manifest.toml:54-56` declares [connector.env_static] with SMOKEBALL_ENVIRONMENT = "staging". The SDK schema has the field (\_sdk/operator_connector_sdk/manifest.py:82) but no consumer in this repo. If the overlay ever applies env_static after staged secrets, a production seat silently gets staging hosts. Either remove the declaration or pin its precedence with a test.

## AC
- [ ] SMOKEBALL_REGION staged explicitly per seat
- [ ] env_static declaration removed or precedence-pinned with a test

issues.title: Document the Smokeball API key source + fix four stale credential/doc references
issues.body:
## Why

The 403 root cause survived six weeks because the one doc anyone reads before staging Smokeball creds is silent on the x-api-key, while our own engagement plans had recorded the answer and were never consulted (IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:146-147, TEST-PLAN.md:122-123 in the engagements repo: "US API key is account-scoped").

## What

1. `operator/verticals/law-firm/smokeball-surface.md:33` — record: the API key is account-scoped per (region, environment); six distinct keys on six gateways (us-east-1 / ap-southeast-2 / eu-west-2); obtained from console.smokeball.com left-nav API section (per-environment tab, "US API Key — Click to reveal"), NOT the Apps credentials card (which shows only client id/secret — the exact mis-copy trap). Rotation is self-serve: API section, Actions, Rotate Key. Usage plan burst 5 / rate 5 is the standard partner allocation; exceed returns 429 (never 403); increases rarely granted; docs conflict on per-endpoint vs global enforcement. The docs example x-api-key value (base64 of client_id:cl) is a placeholder, not a format hint.
2. `operator/bin/provision-customer.sh:844` cites `operator/bin/connect-smokeball.sh`; the script lives at `bin/connect-smokeball.sh`.
3. ss-console#1671 (and engagements#22) describe the firm authorizing "via the portal OAuth connect flow" — no portal flow exists for Smokeball (src/pages/portal/products/operator/oauth/[connector]/index.ts:56 rejects all but google-workspace); the real path is Captain-invoked bin/connect-smokeball.sh (ADR 0054). Correct the wording where it will be read again.
4. `operator/customers/pilot-smokeball/l2/driver.py:51` lists SMOKEBALL_STAGING_API_KEY under "(App 1)", implying app-scoping; seed_staging.py:12 has the correct "(account-scoped)" wording.

## AC
