issues.title: One-time deep pass: narrative accuracy of the 154 tenant memo bodies
issues.body:
Captain-approved 2026-08-02. The 07-31 audit scanned all 154 pilot-tenant memos for **identifier** integrity (0 fabricated numbers, 1 mis-attribution) but explicitly did not check **narrative** accuracy: a memo that mis-describes a matter without naming a wrong number — wrong caption, wrong party, wrong document title, wrong procedural posture — was invisible to that scan (audit §3.10 caveat, §8 open item).

## Shape

For each memo: extract every checkable factual claim (party names, captions, document titles, dates, amounts, procedural events), resolve the bound matter's actual record (matter, files, tasks, events, contacts), and grade each claim as supported / unsupported / contradicted, with the record cited. Multi-agent fan-out is the natural fit; every claim carries the command + output that graded it.

Instrument validity (Law 12): seed the grader with a known-wrong control memo first; if it grades clean, the instrument is broken — stop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (runtime) All 154 memos graded against the live tenant; report with per-claim evidence committed to docs/audits/
- [ ] Contradicted claims escalated to the Captain with the memo id and the record
- [ ] The one known mis-attribution (memo e8a51cf3) appears in the results — the instrument's positive control

**Blocked on #2148** (Smokeball auth down — tenant reads impossible until re-connect). Related: audit §3.10, §8.

issues.title: Recurring accuracy audit: weekly sampled reconciliation of Operator outputs against the source of record
issues.body:
Captain-approved 2026-08-02 (scope: all of it, alongside the one-time deep pass in the companion issue). The permanent loop that measures whether the Operator's stated facts match the systems they claim to come from.

## Shape

A scheduled job samples N Operator outputs per week across **every output class** (external emails, internal memos, digests, calendar/task writes), extracts every identifier, date, and number, and verifies each against the source of record via API — reporting a per-claim disagreement rate with evidence.

Design constraints (Law 12 — the check must be able to fail):
- Include a seeded **false control** each run (one deliberately corrupted claim must be caught, or the run is invalid)
- Sample across classes and skills, not just the chattiest surface
- Verify against the live record, never fixtures or seed scripts (the 07-31 audit's own four wrong calls came from grading against fixtures)
- Output: a dated report artifact + disagreement rows; disagreements above zero page the Captain

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Sampler + verifier + report emitter; runs headless on a schedule
- [ ] (repo) False-control seeding built in; a run whose control is not caught fails loudly
- [ ] (runtime) Two consecutive scheduled runs produce reports; one carries an induced disagreement and flags it — observed, crane_verify recorded
- [ ] Captain-facing: where the report lands (admin console or email) authored, not assumed

Blocked for tenant-backed classes on #2148 (Smokeball auth down). Related: docs/audits/operator-output-provenance-2026-07-31.md §7, #2128, #2132.

issues.title: Capture the verified replying sender on an ack, and write the confirmer as memo content — BEFORE any write-back
issues.body:
Audit remediation item 16 (docs/audits/operator-output-provenance-2026-07-31.md §3.11), previously unfiled.

The client-delivered commitment — "every confirmation is logged on the matter with the attorney's name and a timestamp" — is unbacked: no write-back exists, and the confirming sender's identity is discarded at every layer (the `escalation_append` schema has no actor field under `additionalProperties: false`; the sender is tested as a boolean roster gate then dropped; `auth_mode: authorization_code` means Smokeball `createdBy` is whoever clicked Allow, wrong for any multi-attorney firm).

**Ordering is the point**: a write-back built without sender capture produces an affirmative false record on a legal matter ("Chris confirmed" when Christa replied). Build the capture first; the write-back second; never lean on Smokeball createdBy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) The ack event records the verified replying sender (schema extended; broker-validated)
- [ ] (repo) The matter write-back writes the confirmer **as content** (a memo naming the confirmer + timestamp), never inferring identity from createdBy
- [ ] (runtime) An ack from a rostered sender produces a ledger row naming that sender, and a memo on the right matter naming them — observed, crane_verify recorded
- [ ] (runtime) Negative control: an ack-shaped reply from a non-rostered sender produces no attribution — observed

Related: #2151, #2122 (audit-log actor attribution — peer analysis 2026-08-02), audit §3.11, commitments §6.

issues.title: ACK item identity: derive item_key from stable sources, not model-composed labels; dedupe twin tasks
issues.body:
Audit remediation item 15 (docs/audits/operator-output-provenance-2026-07-31.md §3.11), previously unfiled.

The ACK token store is correct (88/88 recomputed matches, zero collisions) — do **not** rebuild it. The seven-day snooze promise fails because `item_key = sha256(matter_id, source_id, label, authored_date)` and `label` is model-composed free text: 86 fired events produced 83 distinct item_keys, so the same deadline arrives as a new identity daily, and acking today's key leaves tomorrow's unacked. Compounded by duplicate tasks: two source_ids for one obligation mint two keys/codes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `item_key` derived only from stable record fields (matter_id, source_id, authored_date) — no model-composed input
- [ ] (repo) Duplicate-task collapse: one obligation, one key (dedupe on the stable key before raising)
- [ ] (runtime) The same deadline raised on two consecutive days carries the same item_key both days — observed
- [ ] (runtime) An acked item does not re-fire within its snooze window across a day boundary — observed, crane_verify recorded

Related: #1935 (closed — the wrong-codes half), audit §3.11.

issues.title: The agent has no read_file tool, so the authored-spec read can never happen
issues.body:
## The defect

The whole authored-spec mechanism depends on the agent reading a file. It cannot.

Driving a real drafting turn on `hermes-pilot-smokeball` via `/mcp/turn`, the agent replied:

> I don't have a `read_file` tool available in this session — my toolkit includes Smokeball, AgentMail, escalation, and delivery tools, but not a filesystem read tool. I cannot read the authored voice spec, so I cannot proceed.

## Why that breaks the feature rather than inconveniencing it

Every layer of ADR 0083's spec chain is built on that one act:

- `spec_stamp` renders a pointer telling the model **"read this file"**
- `spec_read.py` marks `SPEC_STATUS` on a `read_file` under `${SMD_SPEC_DIR}` — `_READ_TOOLS = frozenset({"read_file"})`, and nothing else sets the mark
- `spec_gate` passes only when that mark exists this turn

So on a seat declaring `voice_spec: expected`, **every `work_product` delivery refuses forever** and no drafting turn can ever satisfy the gate. Fail-closed and correct, for a reason nobody chose — the same shape as the `voice_gate` fleet-freeze in #2086.

## What is already confirmed

- `read_file` **is** classified `READ` in `TOOL_ACTION_CLASS_MAP` (`shared/action_classes.py:469`)
- `read_file` is **not** in the seat's `agent.disabled_toolsets` (browser, computer_use, image_gen, tts, video, video_gen, x_search, homeassistant, spotify, discord, discord_admin, yuanbao, session_search, workspace)
- Hermes' config references `read_file` extensively (pagination caps, char limits) — so the tool exists in the substrate

Unresolved: **which toolset owns it and why it is absent from this seat's surface.** That is the next probe, and it should not be guessed at.

## Everything downstream is proven and waiting on this

Same seat, same session (`vfy_01KZ01EKSFKMDKYD3CSW5H04S0`): spec written to the vault, applier installed it root-owned and hash-verified, pointer stamped without embedding prose, delivery **REFUSED** without a read and **ALLOWED** after a read mark was set programmatically.

The chain works. The agent just cannot perform the one act it is built on.

## A second finding from the same turn

Five tools are unmapped and fail closed to `REFUSED`, and the agent burned a 55-second turn budget calling them:

```
mcp_smokeball_get_prompt
mcp_smokeball_list_prompts
mcp_smokeball_list_resources
mcp_smokeball_read_resource
web_extract
```

Four are the **MCP protocol surface** (prompts/resources), not Smokeball business tools — so every seat with an MCP connector wastes turns on refusals. Worth its own fix; noted here because it was found in the same run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) The toolset owning `read_file` is identified and the reason for its absence recorded
- [ ] (runtime) An agent turn on a proving seat reads a file under `${SMD_SPEC_DIR}` and `SPEC_STATUS` records the mark
- [ ] (runtime) A drafting turn composes against the spec and `smd_deliver_draft` **authorizes** the delivery — the row this blocks
- [ ] (repo) The MCP protocol surface is classified, or deliberately excluded with the reason stated

Related: #2094, #2141, ADR 0083.

issues.title: Voice distillation: assemble the four compilers into one run
issues.body:
The compilers exist and are individually proven. What does not exist is the single command that runs them in order and emits one versioned artifact.

## What is built (all merged 2026-08-01)

| Module | Property it makes unforgeable |
|---|---|
| `operator/bin/spec_leak_check.py` | no sentence was copied |
| `operator/bin/voice_profile.py` | every number was computed, not typed |
| `operator/bin/spec_selftest.py` | no `block` rule refuses output the firm itself produces |
| `operator/bin/spec_fixed_strings.py` | boilerplate is verbatim only where a human approved it |

Method: `docs/runbooks/operator/voice-distillation.md`. Evidence: `docs/research/voice-distillation/2026-08-01-spec-representation-bakeoff.md`.

## What is missing

**1. The artifact split.** Each module emits its own JSON today. The synthesis calls for one keyed set, so a card and the numbers rendered into it cannot drift apart:

```
manifest.json        COMPILER   files + sha256 + labels + date
profile.json         COMPILER   every integer in the system
fixed-strings.json   HUMAN      Layer Zero, per-approval
card.md              AGENT      prose, ZERO integers
gate.json            COMPILER   the exit gate, executable
card.compiled.md     COMPILER   card.md + profile.json rendered together
```

The digit invariant (`voice_profile.card_digit_violations`) exists but gates nothing yet — `test_the_shipped_fixture_would_fail_the_digit_invariant_today` records that gap deliberately rather than letting it look closed.

**2. Held-out validation.** Exclude two documents from the derivation, draft against the compiled spec, grade against the held-out originals with `operator/voice-gate/`. A spec that cannot reproduce a document it never saw is overfit, and nothing tests for that today.

**3. Manifest-hash CI gate.** Any change under a customer's `voice/` that does not update the manifest hash should fail the build. This is what catches the stale-corpus failure that produced every falsified count in the bake-off's reviewed card.

## Not blocked on anything

This is assembly over working parts. The two open questions are elsewhere: the real-corpus validation (below) and the portal paste that closes the last runtime row of #2094.

## The measurement this cannot substitute for

The bake-off corpus is **synthetic and was written to instantiate eight named traits**, so every arm was partly rediscovering a specification rather than discovering a voice. The headline score is an upper bound on a task easier than the real one.

Run the procedure against a real firm's corpus with no trait list supplied, and have the principal grade blind. Until that runs, the representation is chosen on good evidence and the magnitude is unproven — and no completion report should imply otherwise.

Related: #2094, ADR 0083.

issues.title: hermes cron run reports 'Ran now: succeeded' with no observable execution
issues.body:
`hermes cron run <id>` on pilot-smokeball returns:

```
Triggered job: op-managed:operator:deadline-miss-escalator (a726fd5efd24)
  Ran now: succeeded.
```

and produces no observable execution.

## Evidence (2026-08-01, after the ss#2122 reprovision)

Two different jobs triggered, both reporting `succeeded`:

- `deadline-miss-escalator` (a726fd5efd24) at ~21:40Z — its own `Last run` field DID advance to `2026-08-01T14:55:15-07:00`
- `medical-chronology-maintainer` (804e3f3f00cd) at ~22:00Z — `Last run` never appeared

Three independent surfaces show nothing happened:

| Surface | State |
| --- | --- |
| `audit_log` rows after 21:40:15Z | **0** |
| `/opt/data/audit/audit.db` mtime | `Aug 1 21:40` (the boot self-check, not the runs) |
| `/opt/data/audit/escalation-ledger.jsonl` mtime | `Aug 1 19:09` — *before* the deploy |
| `fly logs` grepped for `escalat\|chronolog\|cron\|skill\|turn` | no matching lines |

The audit write path itself is healthy on this image: the boot self-check wrote `LLM_TURN_COMPLETED` rows at 21:02, 21:32 and 21:40Z. So this is not a broken emitter.

## Why this matters beyond the inconvenience

`hermes cron run` is the tool we reach for to prove seat behaviour on demand — it is how a runtime acceptance criterion gets exercised outside a scheduled window. A trigger that reports success while doing nothing observable makes "I ran the job" an untrustworthy signal, which is the same failure class as the silent-empty export in #2122: a green result that carries no information.

It also blocked two runtime ACs on #2122 from being closed in-session.

## Not yet distinguished

Whether this is (a) the trigger enqueuing to the scheduler rather than executing inline, so the work lands at the next natural tick, or (b) the run being silently dropped. `Last run` advancing for one job and not the other does not cleanly support either reading. Someone should determine which before relying on this command again.

A cheap discriminator: trigger a job, then check whether its work appears at the next scheduled tick. If it does, this is (a) and the fix is honest output wording — `Enqueued`, not `Ran now: succeeded`.

issues.title: A fabricated hearing date written to the firm's calendar is invisible to the identifier gate
issues.body:
## The gap

The `record` output class declares `gates: extractive_only` over seams including `smokeball_task` and `smokeball_file` (`operator/contracts/output-classes.yaml:121-125`).

Those seams are **not scanned**. The outbound gate locates a body via `_BODY_ARG_KEYS` (`plugins/hermes-smd-trust/outbound.py:130-140`), and:

- `create_event(subject, start_time, end_time, attendees)` has **no key in that list** — `description` is not among them
- `create_task`'s `due_date` and `subject` are not either

Body-optional plus no recognisable body key means **allowed with no report** (`outbound.py:433-437`).

So a date the Operator composed and wrote straight into the firm's calendar or task list never reaches the provenance check. In a PI practice that is the highest-stakes fabrication there is — a hearing date or an SOL — and it is the one path with no coverage at all.

## Why it matters more after #2127

Pair-keyed provenance now catches a mispaired matter/date **in prose**. It does not look at structured write arguments. That asymmetry is easy to mistake for coverage: the digest is watched, the calendar write that the digest is *about* is not.

Related: the audit found the Operator computed deadlines and wrote them to the tenant as task due dates, then read them back a week later under the framing "authored task due dates read from Smokeball" (`docs/audits/operator-output-provenance-2026-07-31.md` §3.4). #2115 stopped the computing. Nothing yet checks the writing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) The gate extracts identifier candidates from structured write arguments — at minimum `due_date`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `subject` — for body-optional `INTERNAL_WRITE` tools
- [ ] (repo) An unresolvable/absent body on those tools no longer means "no fabrication surface → allow"
- [ ] (runtime) A `create_event` carrying a date not read this session is reported; one carrying a read date is not — observed, `crane_verify` recorded

The second runtime clause is the control, and it matters more than the first: the calendar is written on nearly every routine run, so a gate that flags correct writes would be muted within a day.

## Until this closes

`extractive_only` must not be described as satisfied for the `record` class. It covers prose seams only.

Related: #2127, #2128, #2115, ADR 0083.

issues.title: Seed the provenance register per-record, so pair-keyed provenance is live rather than dormant
issues.body:
## State

#2127 landed pair-keyed provenance in `operator/safety-substrate/identifier_filter.py` — the register can hold `(matter, date)` associations, `check` extracts them per line, and the mispairing that reached the firm on 2026-08-01 is a passing regression test.

**It is dormant on every seat.** `check` consults `has_pairs` before reporting any pair, and nothing seeds pairs yet, so `has_pairs` is false and pair checking is skipped. That gating is deliberate — an unseeded register would flag every digest line carrying a matter and a date — but it means the mechanism does no work until this issue closes.

## What is missing

The read path lives in the overlay: `shared/provenance.py::record_read(session_id, text)` regexes the tool-result **text** into atoms. It must additionally call `ProvenanceRegister.add_record(case_number, dates)` **once per record**, using the fields the connector resolved in code (`matterNumber`, `dueDate`, `start_time`, `end_time`).

Per-record is the whole point and the one thing not to get wrong: `add_read_text` deliberately registers no pairs, because pairing every case in a blob with every date in the blob registers the cross-product and verifies exactly the mispairings this exists to catch. That is pinned by test in #2127.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `record_read` (or a sibling) iterates the records in a tool result and calls `add_record` per record, not per blob
- [ ] (repo) The overlay's vendored `identifier_filter.py` is brought to parity with #2124 + #2127, and the drift detector from #2125 covers it
- [ ] (runtime) On a seat, after a digest run, `has_pairs` is true — observed, `crane_verify` recorded
- [ ] (runtime) A digest whose lines are all correctly paired reports **zero** pair hits (the false-positive control — this matters more than the true positive)
- [ ] (runtime) An induced mispairing reports exactly one pair hit

The fourth row is the one that decides whether this can ever move off report-only. A mechanism that flags correct lines is worse than no mechanism.

## Blocked on

The overlay checkout. As of 2026-08-01 it holds ~307 lines of uncommitted work from a concurrent session on #208's branch. Coordinate before touching it.

Related: #2127, #2124, #2125, #2115.

issues.title: Cross-repo drift detector for identifier_filter.py — the contract test cannot see the file it is a contract with
issues.body:
## The gap, demonstrated

`operator/safety-substrate/identifier_filter.py` declares itself the source of truth; the overlay carries a vendored copy at `shared/identifier_filter.py`. The overlay's `tests/test_identifier_filter.py` calls itself a **CONTRACT TEST** asserting parity.

It cannot. It imports `shared.identifier_filter` — the overlay's own copy — and lives in the overlay repo, so it has no access to the ss-console file it claims parity with. It asserts the vendored copy agrees with itself.

**This is not hypothetical.** On 2026-07-31, overlay #208 added the matter-number alternation to `_CASE_RE` in the vendored copy only. The two files sat out of parity in exactly the direction the module docstring forbids ("changes land there first"), and nothing detected it. It was found by reading, not by CI. #2124 back-ported it.

## Why P1

This file is a safety primitive. Divergence means the gate that runs in production behaves differently from the file we reason about, review, and test against here — and the failure is silent in both directions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) A CI step fails when the two copies diverge behaviourally. Suggested shape: a shared fixture of behavioural cases (input → expected extraction/verification), committed here and executed by both repos, so neither can drift without a red build.
- [ ] (repo) The overlay's contract test is renamed or rewritten so its name matches what it actually asserts
- [ ] (repo) Same treatment for the other vendored primitive, `citation_filter.py`, which carries an identical "keep aligned with ss-console" instruction and the same absent enforcement

## Blocked on

The overlay half. As of 2026-08-01 that checkout holds ~307 lines of uncommitted work from a concurrent session, on #208's own branch. Coordinate before touching it.

Related: #2124, overlay #208.

issues.title: smokeball connector: UpdatedSince is a sunset parameter on /tasks and /matters — migrate to LastUpdated
issues.body:
Found while reading the Smokeball OpenAPI spec (`https://docs.smokeball.com/openapi.json`) during the 2026-08-01 matter-number work — the first time this repo has checked the vendor contract directly.

## The finding

`operator/connectors/smokeball/smokeball_connector/server.py` passes `UpdatedSince` on both `list_tasks` and `list_matters`. The vendor's own parameter description:

> Filter by tasks updated since a specified time (.net ticks representation of the UTC datetime). Cannot be used in conjunction with `LastUpdated`.
>
> **This field will not be supported in future, please use LastUpdated instead.**

It is the only parameter marked this way on either endpoint. Both are among our highest-traffic reads — every digest, every deadline scan, every records sweep.

## Why this is a real change, not a rename

1. **Mutually exclusive.** The spec states the two cannot be used together, so this is a swap, not an addition.
2. **Different types.** `UpdatedSince` is `integer` (.NET ticks); `LastUpdated` is `string`. The connector's format handling is confirmed at connect (`list_matters` docstring: "the .NET-ticks vs ISO format is confirmed at connect") — that confirmation logic is what has to change.
3. **Incremental-sync semantics.** Anything persisting a high-water mark across runs stores ticks today. Check the calendar-sync lookback path in particular.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) `list_tasks` and `list_matters` pass `LastUpdated`; `UpdatedSince` is no longer sent
- [ ] (repo) The connect-time format confirmation covers the new parameter's type
- [ ] (repo) Any persisted high-water mark is migrated or recomputed, not silently reinterpreted
- [ ] (runtime) An incremental read against the tenant returns the same result set the tick-based call did, observed and recorded with `crane_verify`

The runtime row matters here: a sync filter that silently returns nothing looks identical to "nothing changed."

Related: #2047 (connector SDK migration).

issues.title: C1b: declare output_classes on a seat, so the spec gate binds at all
issues.body:
Contract C, the row between #2089 and #2086. Blocked by #2089.

**The gap.** W0′ (#2079) added `output_classes:` to the schema as **optional and default-absent**, which was right for a seams PR. S3 (#2088) then shipped `spec_gate`, which binds only where a seat declares `output_classes.<class>.voice_spec: expected`.

No seat declares it. `vfy_01KYWJKEHY68DHW3NV29QDE813` — the block is absent from all eight `customer.yaml` files.

So the spec loader is built, shipped into the image, root-owned on the volume, gated on a per-turn verified read — **and bound to nothing on every seat.** Built, delivered, inert. The failure class this programme exists to end, arriving inside the programme's own work.

**Why this cannot simply be authored today.** Declaring `voice_spec: expected` for a class whose spec is not installed makes that class's autonomous sends fail closed to draft — correct behavior, and the entire point of the declaration, but it converts silence into a downgrade on a seat that is working. The producer for `vaults/<slug>/output-classes.json` is #2089. Until it exists, no spec can be installed, so no declaration can pass.

**Order.**

1. #2089 lands the console → vault writer.
2. Author a spec for one class on a **proving** seat (`smd-staging` or `pilot-smokeball` — never a `seat.kind: customer` seat first).
3. Declare `voice_spec: expected` for that one class on that seat only.
4. Observe: the spec installs root-owned, the pointer appears in the profile stamp, the gate passes on a read turn and downgrades on a non-read turn.
5. Only then widen — and widening onto `ashton-price` is a client-designated seat, so it is a Captain call, not an agent one.

**The ordering constraint that makes this load-bearing.** #2086 cannot remove `voice_gate` until `spec_gate` actually binds somewhere, because today removing it would un-freeze every autonomous outside send fleet-wide with nothing behind it. This issue is that precondition.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) At least one proving seat declares `output_classes` with one class at `voice_spec: expected`
- [ ] (repo) A test asserts that a declared `expected` class has a corresponding spec key the writer can produce — a declaration with no possible producer is the defect this issue closes
- [ ] (runtime) The spec installs root-owned under `SMD_SPEC_DIR` and the manifest names it
- [ ] (runtime) `spec_gate` observed PASSING an autonomous send on a turn that read the spec
- [ ] (runtime) `spec_gate` observed DOWNGRADING an autonomous send on a turn that did not

issues.title: C3: the Operator captures a correction; it never applies one
issues.body:
Contract C, stream 3. Blocked by #2089.

ADR 0083 §4: a customer authors by saying it, and **a correction is an edit to that output class's property** — which is what makes "you correct it once and it stays corrected" a mechanism rather than a hope. Auditable, visible, surviving restarts, applying identically to every subsequent run.

## Decide the store, do not inherit it

`operator/migrations/0010_voice_corrections.sql` looks purpose-built: `reviewer_user_id` (the person axis), `recipient_cohort` (the audience axis), `priority`, `superseded_by` (a correction is an edit, restorable). Its header calls corrections "deterministic, attorney-AUTHORED, must-apply facts."

**But its named runtime consumer does not exist and never did.** The migration cites `adapter/voice/corrections.py::select_active`; `operator/adapter/voice/` contains `__init__.py`, `diff.py`, `filter.py`, `transform.py`, `tests/` — there is no `corrections.py`. The table is schema with no runtime, and it lives in the **per-customer** D1 on the seat while promotion is portal-side against the **console** D1 and R2.

So: decide fresh. If corrections land in the console D1 where the portal can promote them, `0010` is **retired** — and that makes it a runtime layer needing its own negative probe under "gone means gone", not a silent orphan.

## The agent captures, and never applies

This is the security shape, and it follows from #2084's finding rather than from caution. `read_file` is READ-class, unfenced, and does not taint. A spec the agent could write is a persistent, untainted, self-authored prompt-injection channel surviving restarts. An agent that could promote its own correction into a spec has exactly that, one step removed.

Use the broker's uid-gated verb pattern (`workspace_broker/server.py`'s `suppressed_wake_append`): agent-uid-gated, schema-validated **broker-side**, writes `status='proposed'` only, never touches a spec file, never sets approved. Promotion is portal-side and produces a new vault object plus a recomputed hash — i.e. it goes through #2089's reviewed path.

That gives ADR 0083 its "a customer statement becomes a stored class property" with the agent as a **witness** to the statement, never the author of its own ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Store decided and written down; if `0010` is retired, a negative probe per runtime layer
- [ ] (repo) Broker verb is agent-uid-gated and can only write `status='proposed'`
- [ ] (repo) No path exists by which an agent-originated record reaches a spec file without portal promotion
- [ ] (repo) Promotion recomputes the hash server-side
- [ ] (runtime) The Operator captures a correction stated in conversation; it appears as proposed and changes nothing
- [ ] (runtime) A named administrator promotes it, and the next output of that class reflects it
- [ ] (runtime) It still reflects it after a restart

Related: #2089, #2084, ADR 0083 §4.

issues.title: C1: a named administrator can actually author a class property (rows 1, 2, 4)
issues.body:
Contract C, stream 1. Blocked by #2084.

**Gate rows closed:** 1 (an authoring surface a named administrator can REACH), 2 (a plain-speech statement becomes a stored class property), and the spec half of 4.

**Sentence.** A Named Administrator at the client firm says how an output should be shaped or sound, and the next output of that class arrives that way — without an SMD deploy.

## What stands between them and that today

**The surface is unreachable.** #1966 removed `Advanced` from `SETTINGS_LINKS` before the first client login. A fixed editor behind no link closes nothing — *reach* is the literal word in row 1.

**It is broken by construction anyway.** `resolveEditableConfigFromRow` rebuilds a synthetic `CustomerYaml` from the lossy `customer_configs` projection and runs the strict validator over the whole document. `reconstructFromProjection` injects a deliberately-invalid `hermes_ref` sentinel (`v0.0.0@000…`) designed to fail `checkHermesRef`. It fails for **every** customer, always. That is #1965.

**It persists nothing.** The POST endpoint authorizes, merges, validates, writes an audit row, and returns `status=applied` — no D1 write, no PR, no R2 put. The durable ledger honestly records `submitted` while the user is told `applied`. Unlinked today, so no client has seen it; the code still claims a success that did not happen.

**There is no console → R2 writer at all.** The `CUSTOMER_CONFIG` R2 binding is declared in `wrangler.toml` and referenced nowhere else in the repo. `apply-config.ts` was deleted in `09690c5d` when the R2 reconciler was ripped.

## Build

1. **Dedupe the reconstructors first.** Two exist under different names doing the same job — `reconstructFromProjection` (`src/lib/portal/operator/customer-yaml-editor.ts:666`) and `reconstructProjection` (`src/pages/api/portal/operator/settings/customer-yaml-update.ts:295`) — no shared source, no drift test. Strictly smaller than adding the next field twice, and it retires the class.
2. **Fix #1965** — validate only the editable surface; tolerate the reconstructed locked fields the editor never writes.
3. **Build the console → vault writer** for `vaults/<slug>/output-classes.json`. #2082's publisher is structurally incapable of writing that key, by design: two writers, two key spaces, never the same object. `spec_applier` (#2084) already polls and installs it root-owned, so the consumer exists — this is the missing producer.
4. **Kill the `applied`-when-nothing-was-written redirect.**
5. **Re-link `Advanced` into `SETTINGS_LINKS`.**
6. **Correct three docs** that describe the deleted apply path as present: `wrangler.toml:77-79`, `docs/handbook/architecture-map.md:60`, `docs/handbook/repository-map.md:79`. This is where that path legitimately returns, in a different key space.

## Constraints

- **`customer.yaml` stays git-authoritative.** The portal writes `output-classes.json` and never `customer.yaml`; #2082 auto-publishes the latter on merge, so a portal write there would be clobbered by the next unrelated merge to that slug. This does not reopen #1898.
- **`seat:` and `output_classes:` remain preserve-verbatim** on save (W0′). A client must not be able to relabel their production seat, and raising a spec expectation is a commitment change that moves through a PR.
- The spec's declared sha256 is **integrity, not authentication** (#2084). The writer must recompute it server-side rather than trusting a submitted value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) One `reconstructFromProjection`, with a test asserting a single definition
- [ ] (repo) #1965 fixed: the editor resolves for a provisioning A&P-shaped projection
- [ ] (repo) Console → vault writer for `output-classes.json`, hash computed server-side
- [ ] (repo) No success state reported for a write that did not happen
- [ ] (repo) `Advanced` re-linked
- [ ] (runtime) A named administrator authors a class property on the real seat and the object appears in the vault
- [ ] (runtime) `spec_applier` installs it root-owned and the stamp names it
- [ ] (runtime) The next output of that class honours it, and honours it identically on a second run

Related: #2079, #2082, #2084, #1965, #1966, ADR 0083, ADR 0012, #1898.

issues.title: S4: repoint the voice gate, THEN remove mechanism B — in that order, one release
issues.body:
Contract B. Blocked by #2084. **Runs serial and alone**, after Contract A is live.

**Gate rows closed:** 7 (the gate re-expressed before B is removed) and 8 (B absent from every runtime layer).

## Why this is not a cleanup

Removing mechanism B looks like deleting dead code. It is not. `plugins/hermes-smd-trust/voice_gate.py` is wired (`enforce.py` invokes it on an autonomous outside `external_send`) and fails closed by design. Its pass condition is `VOICE_STATUS.was_applied(session_id)` — a per-turn marker that **only B's transform sets**.

Delete B without repointing the gate and that marker becomes permanently `False`. The gate binds on `bool(voice_library)`, which is authored on **all eight** `customer.yaml` files. Every autonomous outside send on every seat downgrades to draft, silently, forever.

Worth stating plainly because it is the current state and nobody chose it: no seat carries any transform samples (`vfy_01KYTFZP3K6JQY1ZF8JZQAARQX`), so the gate is *already* downgrading every autonomous outside send fleet-wide. Fail-closed and correct, for a reason nobody decided. Registered as `unprobed` in `runtime-controls.yaml` in #2079 — its absence from that ledger was itself an instance of the class that registry exists to expose.

## Order, and it is not negotiable

**1. Repoint the gate.** Same release, before any removal commit.
- Binding: `bool(voice_library)` becomes "this output class declares a voice spec" (`output_classes.<class>.voice_spec == expected`).
- Pass: "spec installed **and** hash matches the root manifest **and** `SPEC_STATUS.was_read` this turn" (#2084 builds all three).
- Reasons extend from `{no_samples, transform_not_applied, gate_error}` to `{no_spec, spec_not_read, spec_hash_mismatch, gate_error}`.
- Keep the `VOICE_GATE_TRIGGERED` action_type, so the audit schema does not move.

**2. Observe that sends still send.** On `hermes-ashton-price`, with a spec installed, an autonomous outside send must still go out. This is a runtime AC and it is the whole point: a regression here is invisible until a client notices the Operator went quiet.

**3. Only then remove B**, with one negative probe per runtime layer — R2 sample prefixes, the volume mirror, the running plugin, seat config. Repo-layer deletion is not removal ("gone means gone").

## Keep, do not delete

The read-in-place bridge (#2071) is **kept and repointed** at distillation: name resolution, connector-side extraction, refusal-on-ambiguity and provenance are all required by the spec-authoring step, which needs the same documents fetched the same way. Only its downstream consumer changes.

`operator/voice-gate/`'s blind-test cohorts re-key to class slugs — its existing three (`client`, `opposing-counsel`, `internal-team`) are already three of the six classes, so a rename rather than a rebuild.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Gate binds on the class's declared `voice_spec`, not on `voice_library`
- [ ] (repo) Pass condition is spec-installed + hash-matches-root-manifest + read-this-turn
- [ ] (repo) `VOICE_GATE_TRIGGERED` audit shape unchanged
- [ ] (runtime) An autonomous outside send still SENDS on a seat with an installed spec, observed BEFORE any removal commit
- [ ] (runtime) The gate observed blocking an output that does not conform to its class
- [ ] (runtime) B absent from R2 sample prefixes — negative probe
- [ ] (runtime) B absent from the volume mirror — negative probe
- [ ] (runtime) B absent from the running plugin — negative probe
- [ ] (runtime) B absent from seat config across all eight customer.yaml files — negative probe
- [ ] (repo) `runtime-controls.yaml` entry updated from `unprobed` to name a live probe

Related: #2079, #2084, ADR 0083, ADR 0028.

issues.title: S3: an authored spec reaches the drafting context, and the read is not optional
issues.body:
Contract A, stream 3. Blocked by #2079. **The one genuine unknown in the plan** — every other stream is plumbing with a known shape.

**Gate rows closed:** 6 (the composing path actually reads it), and the SMD-authored half of 9. **Proving seats:** both.

## The defect

There is no loader. Three independent facts:

- The vault sample reader globs `*.json` only, so a `.md` spec placed in the vault is never read. On `hermes-pilot-smokeball` the volume mirror holds `voice-profile.md` and `drafting-voice-spec.md` — the trait spec that *is* the mechanism — sitting one directory from a reader that cannot see them. (`vfy_01KYTFZP3K6JQY1ZF8JZQAARQX`)
- `SOUL.md` renders identity plus tone bullets. `translate.py::_soul_body`'s own docstring says authored voice material is "consumed at runtime from the same profile directory, not embedded here" — by a consumer that does not exist.
- Four drafting skills condition on *"if the seat carries an authored firm voice profile, apply it"* — a condition no code path makes true (ADR 0083 names this).

## Design

**Two guarantees, two mechanisms. They are not the same problem.**

**Delivery.** `translate.py::_install_persona_skills` already `copytree`s each skill dir — including `references/` — into the per-persona profile every boot. Stamp the profile's `SKILL.md` with a sentinel-delimited section. Precedent: `_send_posture_soul_section`, which exists because an agent that cannot see its authored posture defaults *below* it.

**Stamp the pointer, never the prose.** A boot-frozen prose stamp against a hot-synced spec will disagree, and a confidently-served stale spec is worse than no read.

**The stamp is not trusted.** `profile_dir/skills` is hermes-owned, so an agent could rewrite its own stamp and forge the pointer or hash. The read mark verifies against a **root-owned manifest**, never against anything under `profiles/`.

**Enforcement.** New `shared/spec_status.py`, modeled on the existing `VOICE_STATUS` / `SESSION_TAINT` per-turn markers. Producer: the trust plugin's existing `pre_tool_call` — no new hook, no `overlay-hook-surface.json` change. You cannot make a model read something; you can make not-reading-it fail the send.

**Specs are root-owned, and this is the item not to ship without.** The vault target is hermes-owned by construction; `read_file` is READ-class, unfenced, and does not taint. An agent-writable spec is therefore a persistent, untainted, self-authored prompt-injection channel that survives restarts — strictly worse than a tainted inbound email, which at least fences. This repo paid for it once: `entrypoint.sh` records the self-loopback hole proven live on `hermes-smd-staging` 2026-06-15, where an agent-writable config copy let the agent rewrite its own trust ceiling. The fix was root ownership, not policy.

## Build

- New overlay `spec_applier/` — root poller, sibling of `config_applier/`, reusing its `atomic_write` **including owner/mode preservation**, hash-verified before install, **fail-static** (keep the previous spec, never blank)
- `entrypoint.sh` — fork beside the config applier; export `SMD_SPEC_DIR`
- `operator/safety-substrate/invariants/` — refuse to boot if `SMD_SPEC_DIR` is hermes-writable
- `operator/contracts/env-consumption.yaml` — declare `SMD_SPEC_DIR`
- `operator/contracts/runtime-controls.yaml` — register the poller with a named live probe, or it joins the inert-control pile the registry exists to expose

**Persona voice first.** It needs no customer corpus, so it is provable immediately; firm voice waits on a corpus and on the retention conversation that is the Captain's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] (repo) Spec applier is root-side, hash-verified, fail-static
- [ ] (repo) Stamp carries pointer + hash + precedence, never prose
- [ ] (repo) Read mark verifies against the root manifest, not the stamp
- [ ] (repo) Boot invariant refuses start if `SMD_SPEC_DIR` is agent-writable
- [ ] (runtime) `SMD_SPEC_DIR` observed root-owned and not hermes-writable on a live seat
- [ ] (runtime) A delivered staff-facing output observed in the authored persona register
- [ ] (runtime) Identical on a second run after restart

Related: #2079, #2082, #2083, ADR 0083, ADR 0028.

issues.title: S1: publish merged customer.yaml to R2, and close the unvalidated boot fetch
issues.body:
Contract A, stream 1. Blocked by #2079.

**Gate rows closed:** 5 (property reaches the running Machine). **Proving seat:** `hermes-ashton-price`.

## The defect

`origin/main` carries A&P's authored persona register (#2077). The live seat's config and `SOUL.md` still say `plainspoken / warm-but-professional / concise`. CI syncs `customer.yaml` → D1 only; the sole writer to `vaults/<slug>/customer.yaml` — the object the seat actually reads — is `provision-customer.sh`, run by hand. Merged config sits in git indefinitely. (`vfy_01KYTX7R6SQ7HNX6GWNR607QDF`)

## Build

**The publisher.** New `scripts/ci-publish-customer-configs.sh`, wired into `deploy.yml` beside the existing D1 sync. Mirror `ci-sync-customer-configs.sh`'s shape: diff the push range, publish only changed slugs, stamp and verify.

Two guards, both load-bearing:
- **Never create.** Do not write an object for a slug that has none. A merge must not be able to conjure config for an unprovisioned seat. (Same posture as the D1 sync's Captain-gated first projection.)
- **Structurally cannot write `output-classes.json`.** That key belongs to the portal (ADR 0083, and #1898's principle that R2 must never diverge from git out of band). Two writers, two key spaces, never the same object.

**Close the boot-fetch hole.** `entrypoint.sh` does `aws s3 cp` → `mv -f` with **no validation**; only the poller validates. Auto-publish therefore arms every merge: a live apply the poller rejects leaves the object in R2 to be adopted unvalidated at the next restart — a Fly migration, an OOM, an unrelated redeploy. Validate `${LIVE_CUSTOMER_YAML}.r2.tmp` before `mv -f` and keep the existing file on failure; the `elif` branch already has the shape.

**The negative test publishes and immediately reverts**, asserting the final read. It must never leave a knowingly-invalid object at a boot-read key — as originally drafted that test was a delayed-action seat kill.

## The acceptance criterion is a restart, not a poll

Narrowed deliberately, from the overlay finding in venturecrane/hermes-smd-overlay#201: `personas.*.tone` is **never** live-writable. `tone` is rendered into `SOUL.md` by `translate.py` at boot and the applier does not re-run translate, so admitting it live would report `APPLIED` over a stale system prompt. The register instead arrives via the unconditional boot fetch.

Getting to no-restart means building a translate-refresh on `APPLIED` for persona-scoped paths — a live rewrite of a running agent's profile, with its own blast-radius review. Not this stream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (repo) Publisher diffs the push range and publishes only changed slugs
- [x] (repo) Never-create guard: no object for a slug that has none
- [x] (repo) Publisher structurally cannot write `output-classes.json`
- [x] (repo) Boot fetch validates before `mv -f`, keeps the existing file on failure
- [ ] (runtime) `ApplyOutcome.APPLIED` observed in the `CONFIG_WRITE` audit row — not merely "the file changed", since a rejected apply and a no-op apply are indistinguishable from the file alone
- [ ] (runtime) The authored register present in `/var/lib/smd-config/customer.yaml` **and** in `SOUL.md` on `hermes-ashton-price` after a restart, with no reprovision
- [ ] (runtime) A knowingly-invalid object refused at the **boot** path, seat still comes up on its previous config

Related: #2079, ADR 0083, ADR 0012, #1898.

issues.title: Split-set served discovery: sequential dispatch never completes capture; multi-attachment single-fileId mechanism unproven
issues.body:
Found during the 2026-07-28 A&P drafting prove-out (WS9 split-set intake simulation; full writeup: venturecrane/engagements operator/customers/ashton-price/prove-out/ws9-split-set/RESULT.md).

Test: rfp-set-one split across 3 emails (caption+POS / requests / requests), run through condensed matter-inbox-router + discovery-served-watch instructions on claude-sonnet-5 with simulated Smokeball state.

**Gap 1 — sequential (event-driven) dispatch holds forever.** Across 3 stateless sequential calls the model never fabricated or duplicated (good, fail-closed held) but also never completed the capture: by email 3 ("this completes the set") it still deferred to human reconciliation. No memo, no task, no filing across all three turns. Batched dispatch (all 3 in one poll window) reconciled correctly to ONE capture — so the working mechanism is the router's scheduled-poll batching, and the fix shape for sequential arrivals is likely a pending-parts hold with reconcile-on-next-part or handoff to the scheduled pass.

**Gap 2 — no stated mechanism for N attachments -> one Smokeball file.** file_attachment_to_matter takes one download_url; the batched run invented a synthetic composite fileId to paper over it. Needs a real mechanism (multiple files linked to one capture record, or documented per-part filing convention).

**Prep-answer nuance (already folded into A&P call prep):** letter 10 §9's "scheduled reconciliation pass" (discovery-served-watch --action scan, SKILL.md ~156-161) covers filed-but-uncaptured documents after outages; it does NOT cover split sets, because in the sequential worst case nothing is ever filed. The honest client answer cites the router's poll cadence.

issues.title: Portal: client-operable kill switch + entitlement controls, every change attributable
issues.body:
## Why this exists

**A customer who cannot stop the Operator without calling us does not control it.** That is the product claim the whole Operator SKU rests on: an agent operating inside a firm's systems, on the firm's data, under the firm's authority. Authority that requires a support ticket to exercise is not authority.

Two controls make it real, and both must be client-operable with no SMD involvement:

- **The kill switch.** Immediate stop of all activity, sticky until deliberately resumed. The customer's unilateral exit from any behaviour they did not expect — the control that makes every other autonomy setting safe to try.
- **Entitlement settings.** A named administrator raises or lowers a routine's autonomy within its authored ceiling. ADR 0035 says the product imposes no entitlement defaults; ADR 0075 caps what a dial can reach. Neither is meaningful if only SMD can turn the dial.

Both are only trustworthy if every change is attributable, which is why the audit requirement is part of the control and not a separate feature: a pause nobody can prove happened, or an entitlement change with no actor, is a control that cannot be audited after an incident.

This is substrate behaviour on every seat. Buyers in regulated practice ask for it in diligence as a matter of course, and the answer has to be a demonstration, not a promise.

## Scope (deliberately minimal — Captain 2026-07-24)

Two access levels for the Operator portal surface, no finer role matrix:

- **Read-only**: review the Operator (settings, activity, audit record)
- **Admin**: read-only + change a routine's entitlement setting + pause/resume (kill switch)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Portal pause control: immediate stop of all Operator activity, sticky until an admin resumes; usable by client admins with no SMD involvement
- [ ] Portal entitlement-setting control: admin can change a routine's tier within its authored ceiling (ADR 0075 caps still bind)
- [ ] Two access levels enforced server-side (read-only cannot mutate)
- [ ] Every pause/resume and entitlement change logged with actor + timestamp, visible in the client-readable audit record; SMD-side changes land in the same record
- [ ] (runtime) Proven by performing each act in the client's role on a proving seat, through the identical path a client uses (ADR 0085: "ready for client use does not require a client")

## Notes

- The scalar trust-ceiling endpoint is retired (`src/pages/api/portal/operator/settings/trust-ceiling.ts` returns 410); this is a fresh build against the flag-day entitlement model, not a revival.
- The #788 principal/operator/compliance matrix (docs/specs/operator/dashboard-roles.md) is explicitly NOT in scope; read-only + admin only.
- Related: #1990 (connector-outage alerting), #1978 (M365 channel), #2206 (pause control renders stale state after submit).
- Per-seat admin seeding is engagement work and tracked in `venturecrane/engagements`, not here.

issues.title: infra: expired packages PAT in NODE_AUTH_TOKEN — local npm ci fails (CI unaffected)
issues.body:
## Corrected diagnosis

The original write-up on this issue was wrong about which token is which. Re-verified by fingerprinting each value (SHA-256 prefix, never echoing the secret) and testing each against `api.github.com/user` and the packages registry:

| Token | Fingerprint | `api.github.com/user` | Packages registry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GH_TOKEN` (shell) | `a7f41447…` | **200**, scopes `repo, workflow` | **403** — valid, but no `read:packages` |
| `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (shell) | `9548e5c7…` | **401** | **401** |
| `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (Infisical `/ss` and `/vc`, identical) | `26ba3ace…` | **401** | **401** |

These are three distinct tokens. The earlier claim that the shell `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` "is just the `gh` CLI token" was an inference from its `ghp_` shape and is false — it has a different fingerprint from `GH_TOKEN` and is dead.

**401, not 403, is the tell.** A merely under-scoped token authenticates and gets 403 (see `GH_TOKEN`). Both `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` values fail authentication outright, which means the credential itself is **expired or revoked** — not misconfigured.

## Why nothing broke for months

1. **CI never uses these tokens.** Both `verify.yml` and `security.yml` set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` — the Actions-issued token, which carries `Packages: read` automatically (visible in any job log's permissions block). `npm ci` in CI has been green throughout, including on `af073ce6` today.
2. **Local installs never needed a refresh.** The `node_modules` in the primary checkout dates from 2026-06-27, and each new worktree inherits a copy. Nothing forced a fresh `npm ci` until one was attempted on 2026-07-24.

So a packages PAT lapsed quietly and the only thing that surfaces it is a cold local install. No configuration changed.

## Impact (low)

Local-only, with a working workaround. `npm ci` deletes `node_modules` *before* it fails, so a bare invocation leaves a worktree with no dependencies — that is the sharp edge worth knowing.

Workaround, since both `@venturecrane` packages already resolve at the versions the lockfile pins:

```bash
mkdir -p node_modules/@venturecrane
cp -R /path/to/primary/node_modules/@venturecrane/crane-test-harness node_modules/@venturecrane/
cp -R /path/to/primary/node_modules/@venturecrane/tokens node_modules/@venturecrane/
npm install --prefer-offline
```

## Fix when convenient

Either add the scope to the existing login — `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages` — and store that value as `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` at Infisical `/ss` prod, or mint a fresh classic PAT with `read:packages` (SSO-authorize for `venturecrane` if prompted). No urgency: nothing in CI or day-to-day local dev is blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Infisical `/ss` prod `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` returns 200 from `https://api.github.com/user`
- [ ] Same token returns 200 for `GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@venturecrane%2fcrane-test-harness`
- [ ] `infisical run --env prod --path /ss -- npm ci` completes in a cold worktree

issues.title: ops: Microsoft verified-publisher status for the Operator Azure app
issues.body:
## Why

When a customer's Microsoft 365 admin consents our multi-tenant **"SMD Services Operator"** app into their tenant, the consent screen shows **"unverified / This application is not published by Microsoft"** with a suspicious-app warning. Confirmed live on 2026-07-24 against the `smdopslab` sandbox (see verify ledger + memory `project_m365_sandbox_operator_mail_proven`).

Two problems:
1. **Trust / optics** — a law-firm admin sees a scary "unverified app" banner while granting mailbox access. Wrong first impression at go-live.
2. **Possible hard block** — tenants that restrict third-party multi-tenant apps return `AADSTS650056`; an unverified app is more likely to be blocked pending explicit admin action.

Microsoft **publisher verification** replaces the warning with a verified publisher name and reduces friction/blocks. It's a one-time org-level task that benefits **every** future M365 customer, not just A&P.

## What's required

- [ ] Microsoft Partner Network / Partner Center account (MPN / Partner ID) under SMDurgan, LLC — Captain-owned. (The free verified-partner tier is sufficient for publisher verification.)
- [ ] Associate the MPN ID with the Entra tenant that **owns** the app registration.
- [ ] Mark the app publisher-verified in Entra (App registration -> Branding -> Publisher verification).
- [ ] Populate the app's Publisher domain + Terms of Service / Privacy statement URLs (the consent screen flagged "the publisher has not provided links to their terms").
- [ ] Re-run a consent into the sandbox tenant and confirm the "unverified" banner is gone.

## Open decision - where does the app permanently live?

The sandbox app currently lives in the throwaway `smdopslab` tenant. Publisher verification should be done on the app in a **permanent** home tenant (an SMD/SMDurgan M365 / Entra tenant), not one we may cancel. Decide the permanent home before verifying - likely tied to whether SMD stands up its own production M365 tenant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MPN / Partner ID obtained and associated with the app's home Entra tenant
- [ ] App shows "Publisher verified" in Entra
- [ ] A fresh admin-consent screen shows the verified publisher name with no "unverified / suspicious" banner
- [ ] Documented in `docs/runbooks/operator/ms-graph-azure-ad-setup.md`

## Refs
- memory `project_m365_sandbox_operator_mail_proven` (sandbox proof, 2026-07-24)
- `docs/runbooks/operator/ms-graph-azure-ad-setup.md`

issues.title: operator: trim per-turn tool surface (28.5k of 40k first-call tokens are tool schemas)
issues.body:
## Problem

July cost reconciliation: cache writes are ~70% of Operator seat cost. Request-dump forensics on pilot-smokeball (vfy_01KXKJEEV1R4EPYFKA6J7YDH16): first API call = **40,457 tokens**, of which **121 tool schemas ≈ 28.5k (70%)**, re-written to 5-minute prompt cache every turn. Audit ledger ground truth: only 57 distinct tools ever invoked.

Dead weight identified in the live payload:
- 9 `browser_*` tools, `session_search` (fattest single native schema), `text_to_speech` — zero audit usage, zero SKILL.md references
- 18 overlay `workspace_*` tools on seats with no Google Workspace authority
- 8 AgentMail inbox-admin/destructive tools (never authorable on any seat)

## Fix (overlay PR)

`translate.py` emits `agent.disabled_toolsets` fleet default (Hermes-native subtraction, model_tools.py; unknown names warn+no-op) with `workspace` conditional on `google_auth`; AgentMail `blocked_tools` → native `mcp_servers.agentmail.tools.exclude`. Send/draft/read tools all stay on the menu (ADR 0025 unchanged). `terminal`+`web` stay (SKILL.md references).

**Measured saving (count_tokens on real payload): -7,272 tokens/turn prefix (18%)** for the full variant; conservative shipped variant ~6.5k.

Not in scope (follow-ons): tool_search deferral (bridge-tool calling convention must be verified against the ADR 0075 gate first); variable-middle trim (tool results are 50-90k/turn — delta-sweep/consolidation already filed).

Doctrine: ADR 0021 (config-not-build), ADR 0015 (no core edits).

issues.title: Chase templates must clear the content floor, or the graduated proactive send holds (ADR 0075 Risk 4)
issues.body:
## Context

The proactive outbound relay (#1868, overlay #162, ADR 0075 amendment) re-applies the content-sensitivity floor (ADR 0031) to a chase draft before delivering it — correctly, fail-closed. Verified during the build: a verification-request chase body that says **"please sign and return the verification"** trips the floor's `contract` category and is **HELD** (drafted, not sent).

That means for the graduated client-verification chase specifically, the "auto-handle" commitment does **not** deliver — the send holds on the floor even when the firm has authored `external_send_client: autonomous`. The relay is behaving correctly; the collision is at the **template** layer.

## Decision needed before A&P go-live

Two options (tune the template, never the floor):

1. **Author chase bodies floor-clean.** Rewrite the verification / records chase language to a plain reminder that states the ask without contract/legal trigger words (avoid "sign", "verification", "execute", etc.). Verify each chase template against `content_floor.classify` returns non-sensitive.
2. **Carve the connective verification-request artifact out of the `contract` category**, clause-local — precedent exists (overlay `c410c52` carved standard not-legal-advice / attorney-client disclaimer boilerplate out of the LEGAL category without weakening genuinely-sensitive detection elsewhere).

Option 1 is lower-risk (no floor change) and preferred unless the plain-language rewrite can't carry the ask.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each proactive chase template (client-verification, records, engagement-letter, AR) runs through `content_floor.classify` and returns non-sensitive, OR a reviewed clause-local carve-out is added with a test.
- [ ] A live cron chase under graduated config produces `PROACTIVE_SENT` (not `PROACTIVE_HELD reason=content_sensitive`).

## Refs

- ADR 0075 §"Amendment 2026-07-14 — #1868" → Risk 4
- overlay #162 / ss #1868 (the relay that surfaced this)

issues.title: hosted-agent: confirm-over-channel approval UX — Telegram + email pause/approve/resume (ADR 0071)
issues.body:
The UX substance of **ADR 0071** — how the owner approves a `confirm`-gated external send over the Hosted Agent's channels, and how the agent resumes and completes the send. This is the biggest piece.

## Investigate first
- [ ] Determine the pause/approve/resume primitive: does Hermes expose a native human-in-the-loop pause/resume, or does the overlay implement it? Document the mechanism before building.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a `confirm`-gated `EXTERNAL_SEND`, the agent emits an approval prompt over the same channel that shows recipient + content summary and requests an explicit yes/no.
- [ ] **Telegram:** inline approve/deny action (or reply), allowlisted-user-only.
- [ ] **Email (AgentMail):** reply-to-approve with a signed, single-use, time-bounded token (no bare "reply yes" that inbound spoofing could trigger — must survive the taint model).
- [ ] On approval, the agent completes the original send; on deny/timeout, it does not (fail-safe to not-sent) and records the outcome.
- [ ] The confirm decision + outcome is written to the audit log.
- [ ] Prior-turn / prior-session approvals are invalid (safety invariant #1).

## Verify (done = wired) — the ADR 0071 capability gate
- [ ] Live `confirm` round-trip on **pilot-smokeball**: agent prepares an external send → requests approval over channel → owner approves → agent sends → audit records it. Proven before `confirm` is authored on any paid seat. `crane_verify` with the transcript/audit evidence.

Blocked by: the `confirm` enforcement issue.

issues.title: Operator: agent confabulated a successful Gmail result from a fenced tool error (trust/safety)
issues.body:
On customer-zero 2026-06-17, the principal asked the Operator (via the claude.ai connector) to read smdurgan@smdurgan.com. Every `workspace_gmail_search` call failed with `BrokerError: 'query'` (broker bug, fixed in #1449). The runtime log shows **zero successful searches**. Yet the Operator reported to the principal: *"access succeeds. A search returned 5 message IDs from the inbox with no errors."*

The agent **fabricated** the 5 message IDs and the 'no errors' claim from a failed tool call. The error was returned wrapped in the taint fence (`[UNTRUSTED INBOUND DATA...]`); the agent appears to have either misread the fenced error as data to summarize, or invented a plausible result.

This is a trust/safety issue independent of the broker bug: a governed Operator must surface tool failures faithfully, never invent success — especially on read/summarize tasks a principal will act on. Investigate: (1) how the taint-fenced error reached the agent's reasoning and why it produced a fake positive; (2) whether tool-error results should be presented to the agent outside the untrusted-data fence (an error is not third-party content); (3) a guard/eval that catches 'reported success with no corresponding successful tool call'.

issues.title: operator: BUILD adapter for Microsoft Graph DocumentStorage (OneDrive + SharePoint)
issues.body:
## Source

ADR 0020 connector decision table specifies `build:microsoft_graph` for the DocumentStorage capability against OneDrive / SharePoint. Microsoft has shipped first-party MCP servers for Mail, Calendar, Teams, User, and Copilot Chat — but NOT OneDrive/SharePoint as of this revision. A BUILD adapter is the path until Microsoft ships one.

## Why this is a launch gate

PI firms on Microsoft 365 typically keep matter files in OneDrive or SharePoint sites. Without DocumentStorage on Graph, the AI Employee cannot read intake documents the firm uploads, cannot write demand letter drafts back to the firm's document library, and cannot attach files to outbound mail. The capability is on the critical path for customer-zero.

## What's required

1. Azure AD app registration (multi-tenant) with `Files.ReadWrite` + `User.Read` minimum scopes
2. OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with per-customer redirect handling
3. Token storage on the per-customer Fly volume per ADR 0010
4. Token refresh handling per OAuth lifecycle spec (#789)
5. Python adapter shipped as plugin code in `venturecrane/hermes-smd-overlay` per ADR 0015 + ADR 0020 — either inside `hermes-smd-trust` or as a dedicated `hermes-smd-microsoft-graph` sub-plugin. Covers at minimum: `files.read`, `files.write`, `folders.list`, `files.search`. Not in ss-console; the in-tree `ai-employee/` tree is being retired per the 2026-05-24 realignment.
6. Tool registration via `ctx.register_tool()` at plugin init per ADR 0020 §"Customer.yaml backend resolution at boot"
7. Capability-conformance metadata per ADR 0006 rewrite — sourcing block can attribute "Marcus pulled this from OneDrive"

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Azure AD app registered, app ID + tenant config documented (Captain-owned)
- [ ] OAuth round-trip works end-to-end against a real M365 tenant: consent → callback → token landed on per-customer Fly volume
- [ ] Token refresh path tested under expiry
- [ ] Adapter registers 4+ tools via `ctx.register_tool()`; first agent turn after boot can call each
- [ ] Trust-ceiling enforcement applies (no autonomous deletes, draft-for-review on writes to shared sites — tunable per skill)
- [ ] Decommission cleanup tested (token revocation composes with #820)
- [ ] Integration test against a synthetic M365 tenant in CI (L1 contract test surface)

## Dependencies

- ADR 0015 — Hermes fork posture (plugin-only overlay, code lives in `venturecrane/hermes-smd-overlay`)
- ADR 0020 — connector strategy
- ADR 0010 — per-customer OAuth token storage
- ADR 0006 (rewrite) — capability adapter pattern
- #789 — OAuth lifecycle spec
- Customer-zero gate

## Related

Supersedes part of #822 (the OneDrive/SharePoint portion). Sibling issue #1056 covers the hosted-MCP wiring for Mail/Calendar/Teams.
